articles.title: Rubio Trip Highlights US Push For Deeper Ties With Central Asia
articles.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio departed Uzbekistan on October 20 for India after meetings with all five Central Asian countries, wrapping up a visit aimed at expanding Washington’s economic and diplomatic engagement with a region increasingly intent on shaping its own international partnerships.

articles.title: 'We're Never Going To Be The Major Player': Former Diplomat's Reality Check On US Ambitions In Central Asia
articles.summary: Marco Rubio has brought nearly 300 American business representatives to Uzbekistan for a meeting with representatives of the five states of Central Asia. But Daniel N. Rosenblum, a former US ambassador to Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan, cautions that investment faces major obstacles.

articles.title: Rubio Travels To Central Asia As US Seeks Deeper Trade And Security Ties In Region
articles.summary: As Secretary of State Marco Rubio heads to Uzbekistan, Washington is hoping the high-level diplomatic engagement translates into concrete economic and security cooperation.

articles.title: Rubio Heads To Central Asia As US Seeks Bigger Role In Region Dominated By Russia, China
articles.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio heads to Uzbekistan this weekend for talks with five Central Asian countries as the Trump administration seeks to strengthen commercial ties and expand Washington's strategic presence in the region.

articles.title: As Russian Arms Exports Slide, Central Asia Shops Elsewhere
articles.summary: Central Asian nations are increasingly turning to India, China, Turkey, and Europe for military equipment to reduce their dependence on Russia. Analysts note that this diversification offers greater political flexibility but could create long-term logistical and operational challenges.

articles.title: From Central Asia To Russia For Work -- And Into The Military
articles.summary: Kazakhstan has asked Moscow to help bring home citizens who say they were pressured into signing military contracts to fight in Ukraine. The request puts a fresh spotlight on the vulnerability of Central Asian migrants to Russia’s military enlistment efforts.

articles.summary: The deportation of several Tajik opposition figures from Germany and other European countries, and their subsequent imprisonment, have heightened fears among Tajik oppositionists in exile. Some say they fear not only being sent home but also losing the Western support they once counted on.

articles.summary: The Soviet-era Roghun Dam project has endured decades of uncertainty and opposition. Now major funding tranches appear to have the project on track to transform Central Asia's energy landscape -- and displace tens of thousands of Tajik villagers.

articles.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha said that US President Donald Trump's decision to waive sweeping sanctions against Russia was "indecisiveness," which "sends the wrong message to the aggressor."

articles.title: Ukrainians, Riot Police Clash In Latest Fight Over Recruitment Tactics, Military Morale
articles.summary: A crowd clashed with police and National Guard troops in a Kyiv suburb amid allegations that men were being held and tortured in a private house. The incident highlights growing tensions over Ukraine’s controversial military recruitment practices as it strives to repel Russia’s full-scale invasion.

articles.title: US, Russia, Ukraine To Resume Peace Talks Amid Doubts Over Breakthrough
articles.summary: The United States says it will host new Russia-Ukraine peace talks in Abu Dhabi on November 10-11, but analysts caution that deep divisions over a cease-fire and security guarantees make a major breakthrough unlikely.

articles.title: Trump Says Iran Wants A Deal 'And It Could Happen'
articles.summary: President Donald Trump repeated his assertion that the United States is winning the war with Iran and said that Tehran wants a deal, adding: “It could happen.”

articles.title: US Strikes Iranian Island As Trump Downplays Prospect Of Renewed Conflict
articles.summary: The United States has struck Iran’s strategic Qeshm Island in a series of previously undisclosed attacks. The strike, conducted on the eve of the US midterm elections, was carried out even as President Donald Trump played down the prospect of renewed war and signals hope for a diplomatic deal.

articles.title: Taliban Concerned Amid Reports Of US Deportation Of Afghans Via Pakistan
articles.summary: Afghanistan has asked the US government to “act responsibly” amid reports that it plans to deport dozens of Afghans via Pakistan, possibly in the coming days.

articles.title: Arrests, Resignations, Repainting: Here's What's Happening In Postelection Serbia
articles.summary: Events have moved fast since Student List won Serbia’s parliamentary elections on October 25. Here are some of the notable happenings that have unfolded in the week since former President Aleksandar Vucic was ousted from office after more than a decade in power.

articles.title: After A Crushing Defeat, What Now For Serbia's Vucic?
articles.summary: Former longstanding Serbian leader Aleksandar Vucic has said he’ll “come back” after losing elections in October. But is his future more likely to be in a court dock instead of the court of public opinion?

articles.title: Russian Strikes Kill More Than 30 In Ukrainian Town As Aid Hub Hit Multiple Times, Kyiv Says
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said his country would cease strikes on Russian oil refineries – as demanded by US President Donald Trump -- if the US would provide Kyiv with Patriot air-defense missiles.

articles.title: 'We Escaped Hell': Oleshky Residents Reach Ukraine After Years In War-Torn City
articles.summary: Shaking with joy, relatives of Ukrainians who have endured years under Russian occupation with almost no food, water, or electricity rushed to greet their loved ones in tears in Chernihiv on October 31.

articles.title: 'Every Day Gets Harder': Victim's Family Speaks 2 Years After Serbia's Novi Sad Station Collapse
articles.summary: On November 1, 2024, 20-year-old Andjela Ruman arrived by train in Novi Sad, where her boyfriend was waiting for her. They died together when the station canopy collapsed. Two years on, her parents, Zorica and Zlatko Ruman, speak to RFE/RL about how they have been coping with their loss.

articles.title: Moscow Reports Drone Attack On Nizhny Novgorod As Russian Strikes Cut Power In Ukraine
articles.summary: Moscow and Kyiv traded strikes on November 1, with dozens of drones reportedly destroyed over Russia's Nizhny Novgorod region and energy infrastructure hit in four Ukrainian regions, leaving hundreds of thousands without power.

articles.title: Belarus Holding At Least 22 Political Prisoners In Psychiatric Hospitals, Rights Groups Say
articles.summary: At least 22 people in Belarus recognized as political prisoners by rights defenders face indefinite confinement inside secretive psychiatric hospitals. Cut off from amnesties and pardons, rights defenders warn that these individuals have effectively vanished into a legal "black zone."

articles.title: China, Russia Deepen Arctic Cooperation In Challenge To US
articles.summary: The 31st meeting of the Chinese and Russian heads of government held in St. Petersburg on October 21 was notable for its focus on cooperation in the Arctic, where Beijing and Moscow are increasingly challenging the United States and its allies.

articles.title: Rubio Casts Doubts On Quick Deal To End War In Ukraine, Defends Russian Contacts
articles.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said he was unsure whether a negotiated end to the war in Ukraine was possible, while European officials told RFE/RL the top US diplomat privately expressed doubts that Russian President Vladimir Putin will attend December’s Miami G20 summit.

articles.title: Baku-Ankara Rift Tests Major US And EU-Backed Projects
articles.summary: Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev’s absence from the Ankara summit has brought Turkey-Azerbaijan tensions into focus, raising questions about their impact on major US- and EU-backed transport and energy projects.

articles.title: Food Lines, War Dead: The Way They Live Now In A Frigid Siberian Town
articles.summary: The scene outside Tura's main food store looked like something from the Soviet era: With the mercury at -15 C, residents lined up for hours to pay high prices for staples short supply. The shortages stemmed from geography and negligence, but Russia’s war on Ukraine has taken its toll on the town.

articles.title: As Lavrov Returns To G20, Ukraine, Middle East Highlight Western Divisions
articles.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov's return to a major diplomatic gathering in the United States has exposed widening divisions between Washington and its European allies over how to deal with Moscow as Russia continues its war against Ukraine.

articles.title: Kosovo Protests Grow Over Killing Of Woman Who Pleaded For Police Protection
articles.summary: Protests are spreading across Kosovo after a woman who repeatedly pleaded for protection was killed, allegedly by her brother-in-law. An official investigation found multiple institutional failures, including a prosecutor's refusal to act on a death threat.

articles.title: Marriage Of Convenience: Russia And Iran Deepen Trade Ties, But Their Partnership Has Limits
articles.summary: Moscow and Tehran are expanding banking links and alternative shipping routes to withstand Western sanctions. But shallow waterways, limited port capacity, and the risks of maritime enforcement constrain their ability to keep trade flowing.

articles.title: G20 Diplomats Meet In Atlanta Amid Divisions Over Russia, Ukraine
articles.summary: Foreign ministers from the Group of 20 leading economies are gathering in Atlanta on October 30-31 for talks expected to expose continuing divisions among Western governments over Russia's war in Ukraine.

https://adcmemorial.org/en/news/witnesse.body: Facebook Twitter Вконтакте Elie Wiesel , a survivor of Auschwitz and Buchenwald and the author of the well-known autobiographical novel Night, wrote that “only those who experienced Auschwitz know what it was; the rest will never know.” As Wiesel saw it, “the witness knew then, as he knows now,” that his experience could not be conveyed or fully comprehended by those who had not been in a concentration camp and had not endured torture and humiliation. The author of the testimony asks: “Others will not know, but will they be able to understand?” And yet, despite his doubts, Wiesel “simply could not remain silent.” Reflecting on the destruction of European Jewry by the German Nazis, Wiesel concludes that over the years not only the actions but also the aims of the antisemites changed: if at the beginning of their rule the Nazis set themselves the task of “building a society without Jews,” towards the end they wanted “to leave behind a world in which Jews seemed never to have existed at all.” Violence against people — Jewish men, women and children — was accompanied by the destruction of the very memory of this people, their culture, language and religion. For many witnesses, the struggle against the destruction of memory became the purpose of their lives, an act of resistance. Contemporary antifascists often repeat that “to remember means to resist,” holding events in memory of comrades killed by neo-Nazis. “Memory Is Resistance” is the slogan on the website of members of Memorial who study the history of political repression in the USSR and preserve testimonies of the horrors of the Soviet past. Memory matters to everyone: both to those who refuse to let themselves or others forget the crimes of the past and the suffering of the victims, and to those who take pride in that past. It is not simply a matter of knowing something — Wiesel was right about that — achieving understanding is much more difficult. We can see how declared aims and ideological attitudes continue to change in our own time. From “Holocaust denial” — until quite recently, apologists for German nationalism claimed that Jews had not been exterminated and had themselves invented both the camps and the crematoria in order to slander innocent Germans (there were even claims that Jews themselves had organised the mass murder of Jews to spite the Aryans) — to contemporary proposals by Alternative for Germany not to teach about Hitlerism in schools and instead devote more attention to Bismarck. Germany’s far-right politicians are now closer to the cynical attitude: “Here’s your beer, here’s your ham, and what happened yesterday is in the past” (the ever-relevant words of a song by Yuliy Kim). No one is saying that it did not happen: it did. The only question is how to regard it, how to understand it. The militarist and nationalist Bismarck is, for the AfD, something good, something to take pride in, while schoolchildren need not be told about certain costs of twentieth-century history: enough already, so much has been said about it. The lavish funeral held in Belgrade with military honours for Ratko Mladić, convicted by the Hague Tribunal of crimes against humanity, is a striking manifestation of the contemporary conflict over memory: for some, the victims and witnesses of crimes matter; for others, what matters is the glorification of war criminals. Everyone wants to remember — but they remember different things and understand the past differently. Those who are erecting ever more monuments to Stalin in the Russian Federation obviously want to remind people of him, often making no attempt to conceal the fact that Stalinism was terror. They simply like terror and want to put it back on a pedestal. And they are prepared to remember the Gulag as well — not to deny its existence, but to explain it in their own way, interpreting it within the framework of the “inadmissibility of distorting the history of the USSR.” Thus, for example, one can hold an academic conference in a former Soviet camp, highlighting “examples of the extraordinary courage and patriotism of our compatriots, whose military and labour achievements have more than once become a central theme of academic conferences organised for ten years by the Perm-36 Museum-Reserve.” But telling the history of the Stalinist era as it was seen by those who survived despite the terror, those who neither forgot nor forgave, is treated as extremism. This is why Memorial was banned and the Gulag History Museum in Moscow was closed. It is not memory that is forbidden — it is understanding that is forbidden, precisely what Elie Wiesel and many others sought to achieve through their testimonies. The struggle to foster an understanding that terror and war crimes are unacceptable does not end even when a verdict has been handed down by the Hague (or Nuremberg) Tribunal. Constant efforts are required not only to prevent people from forgetting, but also to show history — including the most recent history — through the eyes of victims of violence, those who suffered, and surviving witnesses. To show their truth rather than the perpetrator’s version: the perpetrator who does not even conceal what he is doing — who may even take pride in it — but who always has an explanation of his own, most often that he was forced to “strike first,” to assert his right to dominance, and so on. The perpetrators themselves are also eager to preserve the memory of violence — in military monuments, bas-reliefs and installations. The voices of those who suffered can be heard in their memories, accounts and testimonies, which must be collected and published, as is being done today by the Kharkiv Human Rights Protection Group’s “Voices of War” project and in human rights reports , which bring together the tragic experiences of Ukrainian women and men who have suffered as a result of Russia’s military aggression. Stephania KULAEVA First published on the Radio Svoboda blog Facebook Twitter Вконтакте

Диловар Ҷафоев 41 сол дошт. Ду манбаи огоҳ аз қазия, ки бо далели амниятӣ нахостанд номашон фош шавад, рӯзи 3-юми ноябр ба Радиои Озодӣ гуфтанд, “маросими дафн 30-юми октябр дар маҳаллаи Гулакен гузашт.” Яке аз мусоҳибони Радиои Озодӣ, ки дар Хоруғ қарор дорад, гуфт, “Диловар Ҷафоев аз ҳамсараш ҷудо шуда, дар Русия танҳо кору зиндагӣ мекард. Қариб як сол пеш бо Вазорати дифои Русия қарордод баста буд. Аз тарафи онҳо ба ҷанг дар Украина фиристода шудааст.” Ба нақли манбаъҳои мо, Ҷафоев шаҳрвандии Русияро надоштааст. Аммо маълум нест, ки пайвастанаш ба артиши Русия ва рафтанаш ба майдони ҷанг дар Украина ихтиёрӣ будааст, зери фишор ё бо ваъдаи пулу тақдими шаҳрвандӣ. Пойгоҳи “Pamir Inside”, ки ҳаводиси вилояти Бадахшонро бозтоб медиҳад, низ навиштааст, замону макон ва шароити марги ӯ, ҳамчунин воҳиди низомиеро, ки дар он хидмат кардааст ё шартҳои қарордодро мушаххас карда натавонист. Инро ҳам бинед: Русия 1400 шаҳрванди дигари Тоҷикистонро ба ҷанг бурдааст Русия моҳи феврали соли 2022 ба хоки Украина таҷовуз кард ва садҳо муҳоҷири одӣ ва зиндониёну боздоштшудаҳои тоҷикро ҳам ба ин ҷанг бурд. То кунун хабари кушта шудани беш аз сад тоҷикистонӣ дар ҷанги Русия алайҳи Украина расонаӣ гаштааст. Бархе дигар ба дасти низомиёни украинӣ асир афтода, хоҳони раҳоӣ ҳастанд. Радиои Озодӣ аз аввали имсол дар бораи кушта шудани дастикам панҷ шаҳрванди Тоҷикистон гузориш дод. Ҳадди ақал яке аз онҳо, Олимҷон Бердиев , ба ваъдаи тақдими шаҳрвандии Русия ба артиш ва сипас ҷанг рафтааст. Наздиконаш гуфтанд, хабари марги ӯро баъди беш аз ёздаҳ моҳи бедарак буданаш фаҳмиданд, вале то ҳол пайкар ё ҷасадашро ба Тоҷикистон наовардаанд. Қонунҳои Тоҷикистон барои ширкат дар ҷангҳои хориҷӣ аз дувоздаҳ то бист сол зиндон муқаррар кардааст, вале мақомот мегӯянд, нисбат ба касе барои ширкат дар ҷанги Украина парвандаи ҷиноятӣ боз накардаанд. Вазири корҳои дохилӣ Рамазон Раҳимзода моҳи июл дар нишасти хабарӣ дар Душанбе гуфт, "ин ки чӣ қадар аз шаҳрвандони мо дар ҷанги Украина ҷанг карда истодаанд ё наистодаанд, мо ягон ҳисобот намебарем ва дар ин масъала ягон уҳдадорӣ ҳам надорем." Ба иттилои “Зистан мехоҳам”, тарҳи давлатии Украина, мақомоти Русия аз соли 2022 то кунун зиёда аз 5 ҳазор шаҳрванди Тоҷикистонро бо ваъдаи маоши баланду тақдими шаҳрвандӣ ва ё таҳдиди ба зиндон андохтан ё ихроҷ аз қаламрави ин кишвар ба артиш ва ширкат дар ҷанги Украина ҷалб кардаанд. Русия моҳи феврали соли 2022 ба хоки Украина ҳамла кард ва даргирии ду тараф аз он замон идома дорад. То кунун миллионҳо нафар дар Украина бехонаву дар ва паноҳҷӯ шуда, манзилу иншооти зиёде вайрон гаштааст. Маскав ҷанги худро дар қаламрави Украина амалиёти вижаи низомӣ, аммо Украинаву ҳампаймонҳои ғарбияш таҷовуз ба хоки ин кишвар меноманд. Ҳамла ҳамагӣ чанд соат пеш аз оғози интихоботи миёндавраӣ ба Конгресси Амрико ин тахминҳоро ба вуҷуд овардааст, ки дар пайи интихобот амалиёти ҳарбӣ ба муқобили Эрон аз сар гирифта хоҳад шуд. Президент Доналд Трамп оғози фаврии амалиёти густурдаи низомиро аз эҳтимол дур донист ва ба имкони созиш ишора кард. Доналд Трамп Ӯ афзуд: "Мо дар набард бар Эрон дастболо ҳастем. Нерӯи дарёии онҳо маҳв шуд. Нерӯи ҳавоӣ маҳв шуд. Ҳавопаймоҳои онҳо дар фурудгоҳҳои Эрон пора-пора шудаанд. Қудрати мудофиаи зиддиҳавоӣ ва имконоти тавлиди мушакҳои онҳо бисёр поин бурда шудааст. Ба қавли низомиёни Амрико, ҳамлаи ахир яке аз чунин қадамҳост, ки бо ҳадафҳои дифоӣ роҳандозӣ мешавад ва бояд таҳдиди Эрон ба равуои киштиҳои тиҷориро дар оброҳаи Ҳурмуз заиф намояд. Расонаҳои эронӣ рӯзи 3-юми ноябр дар бораи ҳамла ба ҷазираи Қишм хабар доданд. Пайвандҳои дастрасӣ Ҷаҳиш ба мояи аслӣ Ҷаҳиш ба феҳристи аслӣ Ҷаҳиш ба ҷустор Баъдӣ Пӯшонед Пешӣ Баъдӣ Тасвир саҳнаҳое дорад, ки шояд барои дигарон нофорам бошанд. Пардабардорӣ Пайванд нусхабардорӣ шуд ТАРҲҲО Русский Моро пайгирӣ кунед Ҳамаи сомонаҳои RFE/RL Ҷустуҷӯ РУС TV TV Ҷустуҷӯ Пешӣ Баъдӣ Хабари нав Ҷанги Украина Ноябр 03, 2026 Ҳамлаҳо, шубҳа ва ихтилофҳо. Амрико, Русия ва Украина музокиротро аз сар мегиранд? Пайомадҳои ҳамлаи Русия ба Днепри Украина. 3-юми ноябри 2026 Нерӯҳои Русия рӯзи дувуми ноябр бо ҳамла ба як мактаб дар вилояти Запорожйеи Украина, ки дар онҷо ёриҳои башардӯстона тақсим мешуд, ба 31 касро куштаанд. Раисҷумҳури Украина Владимир Зеленский онро "разилона" хонд. Мақомоти Украина 3-юми ноябр гуфтанд, ҳамлаҳои Русия ба як бемористон дар Харков низ дастикам 62 нафарро захмӣ карда, ба зербунёдҳои энержӣ дар гӯшаҳои дигар осеб расонд. Зеленский гуфт, Маскав шаби 3-юми ноябр ба Украина бо 365 паҳподу мушак зарба зад. Вай дар шабакаи "X" навишт, "ин ки ҳамаи ҳодисаҳо дар рӯзи интихоботи Конгресси Амрико рӯй доданд, баёнгари бисёр чиз аст." Вазири корҳои хориҷии Украина Андрей Сибиҳа гуфт, шаби гузашта дастикам 13 иншооти энержӣ дар нӯҳ вилояти Украина мавриди ҳамла қарор гирифтанд. Вай навишт: " Путин барқасдона зербунёдҳои барқу гармидиҳиро ҳадаф қарор дода, умедвор аст, ки пеш аз фаро расидани зимистон шароити мардумро тоқатфарсо мекунад. Ин яке аз таърифҳои дурусти наслкушӣ аст." Дар ҳамин ҳол, ҳавопаймоҳои бесарнишини Украина ба як корхонаи коркарди нафт дар шаҳри Ярославли Русия зарба задаанд. Стив Виткофф Иёлоти Муттаҳида мегӯяд, рӯзҳои 10 ва 11-уми ноябр ҳайатҳои Украина ва Русияро барои даври нави музокирот дар Абузабӣ (Имороти Муттаҳидаи Арабӣ) гирди ҳам меорад. Ҳадаф поён бахшидан ба ҷанги Русия алайҳи Украина аст ва Вашингтон талош дорад аз натиҷаи оташбаси муваққатии ҳафтаи гузашта дар Олешкии Украина , ки зери ишғоли нерӯҳои Русия аст, истифода кунад. Стив Виткофф, фиристодаи вижаи Иёлоти Муттаҳида, 2-юми ноябр аз баргузории ин нишаст хабар дод ва гуфт, Амрико гуфтушунидеро миёнравӣ мекунад, ки ба "тартиботи амниятии пас аз ҷанг, коҳиши танишҳо, талошҳои башардӯстона ва қадамҳои баъдӣ ба сӯйи сулҳ" тамаркуз хоҳад кард. Баъзе аз таҳлилгарон ва мансабдорони пешини амрикоӣ дар суҳбат бо Радиои Озодӣ ҳушдор доданд, ки аз нишасти Абузабӣ набояд интизори пешрафти бузург буд. Онҳо ба ихтилофи амиқи байни Маскав ва Киев, инчунин, набудани нишонаи рӯшан дар мавриди омодагии Путин барои пазируфтани оташбас ишора карданд. Инро ҳам бинед: Помпео: Путин ба поён додани ҷанг дар Украина майле нишон надодааст Вилям Тейлор, сафири собиқи Иёлоти Муттаҳида дар Украина дар замони президенти пешин Ҷорҷ Буш ва сипас кордори сафорати Амрико дар давраи аввали раёсати ҷумҳурии Доналд Трамп, суол гузошт, ки "оё Путин тасмим гирифтааст, ки ба оташбас розӣ шавад?" Вашингтон ва Киев борҳо аз оташбас ҷонибдорӣ карда, Доналд Трамп низ қаблан оташбасро дар бахши энержӣ пешниҳод карда буд. Тейлор мегӯяд, Украина онро пазируфт, аммо Русия не. Владимир Путин, раисҷумҳури Русия, борҳо гуфтааст, ки ҷанг танҳо пас аз расидан ба созиши комили сулҳ метавонад бас шавад. Вилям Тейлор. Акс аз соли 2023 Ба гуфтаи Тейлор, дар ҷараёни нишастҳои пешини сеҷонибаи сатҳи коршиносон дар моҳҳои январ ва феврали имсол, музокиракунандагон дар масъалаҳои техникӣ (фаннӣ), аз ҷумла чигунагии назорати эҳтимолии оташбас, пешрафт карданд. Аммо онҳо натавонистанд бар сари худи оташбас ба тавофуқ бирасанд. "Бахши душвор ва нуқтаи чархиш он хоҳад буд, ки Путин бигӯяд: бале, ӯ ба оташбас розӣ шудааст," – гуфт Вилям Тейлор ба Радиои Озодӣ. Талошҳои нави дипломатӣ барои поён додан ба ҷанги Русия дар Украина дар ҳоле сурат мегирад, ки оташбаси ҳафтаи гузашта бо миёнравии Амрико дар шаҳри Олешкии Украина то андозае дастёбиро ба созиши васеътар умедвор кардааст. Аммо Кремл ишора кардааст, ки ин амалиёт ҳанӯз маънои омодагии Маскавро барои пазируфтани оташбаси фарогир надорад. Диловар Ҷафоев 41 сол дошт. Ду манбаи огоҳ аз қазия, ки бо далели амниятӣ нахостанд номашон фош шавад, рӯзи 3-юми ноябр ба Радиои Озодӣ гуфтанд, “маросими дафн 30-юми октябр дар маҳаллаи Гулакен гузашт.” Яке аз мусоҳибони Радиои Озодӣ, ки дар Хоруғ қарор дорад, гуфт, “Диловар Ҷафоев аз ҳамсараш ҷудо шуда, дар Русия танҳо кору зиндагӣ мекард. Қариб як сол пеш бо Вазорати дифои Русия қарордод баста буд. Аз тарафи онҳо ба ҷанг дар Украина фиристода шудааст.” Ба нақли манбаъҳои мо, Ҷафоев шаҳрвандии Русияро надоштааст. Аммо маълум нест, ки пайвастанаш ба артиши Русия ва рафтанаш ба майдони ҷанг дар Украина ихтиёрӣ будааст, зери фишор ё бо ваъдаи пулу тақдими шаҳрвандӣ. Пойгоҳи “Pamir Inside”, ки ҳаводиси вилояти Бадахшонро бозтоб медиҳад, низ навиштааст, замону макон ва шароити марги ӯ, ҳамчунин воҳиди низомиеро, ки дар он хидмат кардааст ё шартҳои қарордодро мушаххас карда натавонист. Инро ҳам бинед: Русия 1400 шаҳрванди дигари Тоҷикистонро ба ҷанг бурдааст Русия моҳи феврали соли 2022 ба хоки Украина таҷовуз кард ва садҳо муҳоҷири одӣ ва зиндониёну боздоштшудаҳои тоҷикро ҳам ба ин ҷанг бурд. То кунун хабари кушта шудани беш аз сад тоҷикистонӣ дар ҷанги Русия алайҳи Украина расонаӣ гаштааст. Бархе дигар ба дасти низомиёни украинӣ асир афтода, хоҳони раҳоӣ ҳастанд. Радиои Озодӣ аз аввали имсол дар бораи кушта шудани дастикам панҷ шаҳрванди Тоҷикистон гузориш дод. Ҳадди ақал яке аз онҳо, Олимҷон Бердиев , ба ваъдаи тақдими шаҳрвандии Русия ба артиш ва сипас ҷанг рафтааст. Наздиконаш гуфтанд, хабари марги ӯро баъди беш аз ёздаҳ моҳи бедарак буданаш фаҳмиданд, вале то ҳол пайкар ё ҷасадашро ба Тоҷикистон наовардаанд. Қонунҳои Тоҷикистон барои ширкат дар ҷангҳои хориҷӣ аз дувоздаҳ то бист сол зиндон муқаррар кардааст, вале мақомот мегӯянд, нисбат ба касе барои ширкат дар ҷанги Украина парвандаи ҷиноятӣ боз накардаанд. Вазири корҳои дохилӣ Рамазон Раҳимзода моҳи июл дар нишасти хабарӣ дар Душанбе гуфт, "ин ки чӣ қадар аз шаҳрвандони мо дар ҷанги Украина ҷанг карда истодаанд ё наистодаанд, мо ягон ҳисобот намебарем ва дар ин масъала ягон уҳдадорӣ ҳам надорем." Ба иттилои “Зистан мехоҳам”, тарҳи давлатии Украина, мақомоти Русия аз соли 2022 то кунун зиёда аз 5 ҳазор шаҳрванди Тоҷикистонро бо ваъдаи маоши баланду тақдими шаҳрвандӣ ва ё таҳдиди ба зиндон андохтан ё ихроҷ аз қаламрави ин кишвар ба артиш ва ширкат дар ҷанги Украина ҷалб кардаанд. Русия моҳи феврали соли 2022 ба хоки Украина ҳамла кард ва даргирии ду тараф аз он замон идома дорад. То кунун миллионҳо нафар дар Украина бехонаву дар ва паноҳҷӯ шуда, манзилу иншооти зиёде вайрон гаштааст. Маскав ҷанги худро дар қаламрави Украина амалиёти вижаи низомӣ, аммо Украинаву ҳампаймонҳои ғарбияш таҷовуз ба хоки ин кишвар меноманд. Акс аз моҳи марти 2026 Аз 3-юми ноябр дар Русия баҳонаҳои аз ин кишвар берун кардани шаҳрвандони хориҷӣ ё муҳоҷирон ду баробар бештар шуд. Акнун муҳоҷиронро метавонанд барои итоат накардан ба талаби полису марзбон, нашри маводи таҳқиркунандаи шахс дар интернет, вайрон кардани тартиботи ҷамъиятӣ, таҳқири артиш, даъват ба ҷорӣ кардани таҳрими зидди Русия, табъиз ва маҳдуд кардани озодии инсон низ метавонанд ҷарима баста, аз Русия ихроҷ кунанд. Қарор дар бораи афзоиши баҳонаҳои депорти хориҷиҳо дар доираи такмили сиёсати муҳоҷирати Русия сурат гирифта, моддаҳои ҷазодиҳандаро дар Кодекси ҳуқуқвайронкунии маъмурӣ аз 22 то 45 афзудаанд. Вячеслав Володин, раиси Думаи давлатӣ ё порлумони Русия чанд рӯз пеш аз эътибор пайдо кардани ин тағйирот гуфт, қонунҳои нав ба беҳбуди амнияти иҷтимоӣ ва танзими муҳоҷират мусоидат мекунад. Думаи давлатӣ дар ду-се соли охир даҳҳо қонуну муқаррароти зидди муҳоҷиронро қабул кард. Ангезаи расмии он – ҳамла ба толори консертии "Крокус" дар баҳори соли 2024 буд, ки иҷрокунандагони онро асосан шаҳрвандони Тоҷикистон номиданд. Баъзе аз онҳо ва наздиконашон иттиҳомро напазируфтанд. Ҳамзамон чунин андешае ҳам вуҷуд дорад, ки мавзӯи муҳоҷирон дар Русия, ки инак беш аз панҷ сол аст даргири ҷанги бедурнамое бо Украина шудаву харҷи зиндагӣ барои аҳолии маҳаллиаш сангинтар мешавад, мехоҳад бо мавзӯи муҳоҷират таваҷҷӯҳро аз ҷанг дур барад. Қарору маҳдудиятҳои нав барои муҳоҷирон бо ин тамом намешаванд ва аз 1-уми январи соли 2027 баъзе аз қонунҳои нав, масалан, пардохти ҳатмии молиёт (андоз) барои ҳамсар ва фарзандони муҳоҷирон ҳам ба иҷро медарояд. Доналд Трамп дар як гирдиҳамоии интихоботӣ дар аёлати Айова рӯзи 1-уми ноябр гуфтааст, то кунун ба далели талош барои наҷоти ҷони мардум, аз задани зарбаи ниҳоӣ ба Эрон худдорӣ кардааст. Дар сурати зарурат, афзудааст ӯ, иқдоми низомии сангин анҷом хоҳад дод. Вай иддао кардааст, ки тавоноии низомӣ ва барномаи ҳастаии Эрон ба шиддат суст шудаанд ва ин рӯёрӯӣ ба зудӣ поён хоҳад ёфт. Трамп ҳамчунин гуфтааст, талош мекунад шахсеро дар сохтори раҳбарии Эрон барои музокира пайдо кунад. Дар ҳамин ҳол, мақомоти эронӣ рӯзи 2-юми ноябр, пас аз гуфтугӯ бо миёнравоне, ки барои поён додани ҷанг бо Иёлоти Муттаҳида талош доранд, Қатарро тарк кардаанд. Аз сӯи дигар, шабакаи 12-и Исроил гузориш додааст, ки Бенямин Нетаняҳу, сарвазири Исроил, аз Трамп хостааст ҷангро алайҳи Эрон пас аз интихоботи миёндавраии Амрико аз сар бигирад; аммо раисҷумҳури Амрико хоҳони фурсати бештар барои идомаи музокироти дипломатӣ аст. https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2.body: Tanzanian authorities have failed to hold anyone accountable for the violence security forces inflicted on protesters, which left hundreds of people dead and thousands of others injured in the wake of the 2025 general election, Amnesty International said on the first anniversary of the crackdown. Instead of delivering justice and accountability, authorities have withheld a Commission of Inquiry report from the public and intensified attacks on civic space through the abuse of counterterrorism laws. Not a single official has been criminally investigated, let alone prosecuted and punished for the excessive force that Tanzanian security forces used against protesters. In fact, the situation has only deteriorated since the crackdown began. In a classic tactic pulled out of the authoritarian playbook, the authorities are increasingly weaponizing counterterrorism laws to silence critics and instil fear,” Tigere Chagutah, Amnesty International’s Regional Director for East and Southern Africa The organization has documented how, over the past year, security agencies have committed human rights violations with impunity against government critics, opposition supporters, media organizations, and dissenting members of the ruling party. These include acts that may amount to torture or other ill-treatment, arbitrary arrests, enforced disappearances, abductions, and severe restrictions of freedom of expression and peaceful assembly. “Not a single official has been criminally investigated, let alone prosecuted and punished for the excessive force that Tanzanian security forces used against protesters. In fact, the situation has only deteriorated since the crackdown began. In a classic tactic pulled out of the authoritarian playbook, the authorities are increasingly weaponizing counterterrorism laws to silence critics and instil fear,” said Tigere Chagutah, Amnesty International’s Regional Director for East and Southern Africa. Although the Commission of Inquiry report into the 2025 election-related killings was handed over to President Samia Suluhu in April 2026, it has yet to be made public. She has repeatedly alleged that the post-election protests were funded by foreign actors in a bid to overthrow the government. In August 2026, President Suluhu inaugurated another Commission of Inquiry to identify those who planned, funded, coordinated, or executed the violence, as well as investigate the excessive use of force and the whereabouts of missing persons. “President Suluhu’s continued refusal to release the Commission of Inquiry report not only entrenches a culture of secrecy, but it also perpetuates impunity,” said Tigere Chagutah. “It is imperative that this new commission comprehensively address the role of security forces in the election-related crackdown. Its investigations must be thorough, independent, impartial, and transparent. On concluding its mandate, it must ensure its findings are made public immediately.” President Suluhu’s continued refusal to release the Commission of Inquiry report not only entrenches a culture of secrecy, but it also perpetuates impunity. Tigere Chagutah Between 3 and 17 September 2026, Amnesty International interviewed 17 people, including victims of arbitrary arrests, enforced disappearances and abductions, as well as journalists, opposition officials, lawyers, and friends and relatives of the victims of the October 2025 election-related crackdown. Amnesty International also verified charge sheets for those arbitrarily arrested and charged with terrorism in different parts of the country. Tanzanian authorities did not respond to Amnesty’s request for comment. Abductions, enforced disappearances and torture or other ill-treatment Amnesty International documented numerous cases of individuals being abducted by suspected state security officers, held incommunicado, and later charged in court. Some of them remain missing. Among them is Ibrahim Myovella, a youth leader from the opposition party CHADEMA. He went missing alongside two friends on 18 April 2026, after reporting to Central Iringa police station as per their bail conditions following allegations of involvement in the October 2025 protests. The authorities deny ever holding them. Also missing is Mashaka Nestory Kindikwa, 37, a former official of the ruling Chama cha Mapinduzi (CCM) who was abducted from his home and led away blindfolded by seven men believed to be security officers on 25 June 2026. The police have denied holding him. On 20 May 2026, David Djumbe, personal assistant to opposition leader Tundu Lissu, was abducted near his Dar es Salaam home by people believed to be state security officers and subjected to severe beatings which may amount to torture or other ill-treatment. He escaped. Police denied involvement and said they had opened an investigation, but there has been no update on progress or findings. Stefano Patrick*, 26, who expressed support for protests on Saba Saba Day, a national public holiday commemorating the pivotal moment in Tanzania’s struggle for independence, was arbitrarily arrested on 24 July in Dar es Salaam, and detained for 47 days without being charged in court. He told Amnesty International that during his detention, he was tortured and beaten, while also denied food and water. He said his interrogators demanded to know who was funding the protests: “I was blindfolded... but I could hear some people crying in the next room. Some officers came to me and said, ‘Can you hear how your friends are crying, if you don’t cooperate, we will kill you,’. “On the first day, they didn’t give me food. When I asked for water, they urinated on my blindfolded face and said ‘that is the price for those of you opening your mouths to make noise’. I was blindfolded... but I could hear some people crying in the next room. Some officers came to me and said, ‘Can you hear how your friends are crying, if you don’t cooperate, we will kill you. Stefano Patrick* “On the second day, I was taken to Gogoni police station where they beat your legs until they get numb but then insist that you must stand. I saw another person’s legs broken at the police station. Even though I was in trouble, I felt pity for what other people were going through”. Misuse of counterterrorism laws to target critics Amnesty International documented the frequent abuse of counterterrorism laws to target opposition supporters and government critics. On 9 July 2026, police spokesman David Misime said 130 people had been arrested for allegedly organizing meetings and preparing and circulating messages that encouraged criminal acts aimed at destabilizing the country. Of these, at least 64 were charged under the Prevention of Terrorism Act, an unbailable offence. In April 2026, Pendo Jonas Kileo went missing. For two months, the family of the CHADEMA member from Temeke, did not know of her whereabouts. On 27 July, they learned that alongside another CHADEMA member, Kileo had been charged in Temeke District Court with conspiracy to commit terrorist acts as well as participating in terrorist meetings between September 2025 and July 2026. On 4 July 2026, police arbitrarily arrested university students and CHADEMA student-body members Noah Mwalwange, Gwamaka Mboka, Augustino Wasinyo and Rojas Mpani. They were held at Mbeya Central Police Station until 23 July, when they were charged under the Prevention of Terrorism Act. A source familiar with their case said they were denied access to lawyers, beaten with batons during interrogation, stripped, and forced to record confessions and name CHADEMA leaders as their financiers. By resorting to terrorism-related charges against its perceived critics, the Tanzanian government is sending a chilling message that it won’t stop at anything in its effort to repress any and all dissenting opinions. Responding to the European Commission’s proposed reform of the European Border and Coast Guard Regulation (the Frontex Regulation) that vastly expands the agency’s budget, powers, staff and mandate, without commensurately expanding its human rights safeguards and transparency obligations, Eve Geddie the Director of Amnesty International’s European Institutions Office said: “The European Commission’s proposed changes to the Frontex mandate once again prioritize expanding the agency’s powers to deport, enforce border control, and operate beyond the EU without expanding the agency’s human rights obligations in turn. “This includes giving Frontex new powers to carry out forced returns between non-EU countries, paving the way for a broader role in ‘return hubs’ in third countries. This reform compounds the risk of EU complicity in human rights violations and raises further hurdles to transparency and accountability. It should be rejected outright. “Time and again we see the European Commission doubling down on Fortress Europe – increasing border security, surveillance and deportations without ever questioning the growing powers of an agency that has facilitated the trapping of people in human rights abuses. “Frontex’s mandate explicitly requires respect, protection and promotion of human rights. Yet instead of addressing structural deficiencies and flawed approaches that fuel violations and abuses against people at Europe’s borders, today’s decision will turbocharge this flawed approach in countries outside the EU. “As people across Europe protest over access to housing, and underfunding of education and public services, the European Commission continues to present migration control as the continent’s existential challenge, and to disproportionately pour resources into deportations and border enforcement. A fundamental reassessment of its priorities is long overdue.” Background On 27 October, the European Commission presented two proposals : an amendment to the European Border and Coast Guard Regulation increasing the number of Frontex officers to 30,000, giving the agency a greater role in returns and ‘crisis response’, as well as a regulation to digitalize return, readmission and reintegration procedures. Amnesty International has long followed the work of Frontex, acting as a member of its Consultative Forum on Fundamental Rights from its inception in 2012 until the end of 2022. A series of reforms of Frontex have rapidly expanded its powers, budget, and operational capacity since its creation in 2004, with its budget ballooning to over €1 billion annually for 2026. Amnesty International has raised concerns over the role of Frontex’s maritime aerial surveillance activities in the Mediterranean in illegal interceptions of refugees and migrants by the Libyan Coast Guard . Amnesty International has also consistently questioned Frontex’s continuation of operations in EU countries adopting practices that are incompatible with EU law on asylum and migration, urging it to take swift action in cases of reported or alleged fundamental rights violations, and to initiate proceedings in line with the requirements in Article 46 of the existing Frontex Regulation to suspend or terminate its operations in such cases.

Reacting to yesterday’s announcement by the Dutch public broadcasting organization, NPO, that they would not take part in the Eurovision Song Contest in 2027 due to the Israel’s continued participation, Amnesty International’s Europe Director, Steve Cockburn, said: “The Dutch broadcasting body is the latest to decide not take part in the 2027 Eurovision Song Contest in protest at Israel’s participation. It sends a clear message that there should be no stage provided to whitewash genocide, ethnic cleansing and apartheid against Palestinians. It also highlights the European Broadcasting Union’s cowardly refusal to suspend Israel from the competition. There should be no stage provided to whitewash genocide, ethnic cleansing and apartheid against Palestinians Steve Cockburn, Amnesty International’s Europe Director “Israel’s participation in Eurovision offers the country a platform to try to deflect attention from and normalize its ongoing genocide in the occupied Gaza strip and its accelerated annexation measures and ethnic cleansing in the occupied West Bank. “Amnesty calls on the European Broadcasting Union and its members and associates to suspend Israel from the Eurovision Song Contest. There should be no stage for whitewashing genocide.” For more information contact [email protected] Background After consulting broadcasters, the NPO which oversees public broadcasting in The Netherlands, found there was insufficient support for participation, citing “sensitivities” over Israel’s participation in the competition for its decision to pull out.

African leaders attending the Russia-Africa summit must call on the Russian authorities to immediately end the coercive and deceptive recruitment of African nationals into Russia’s military forces to fight against Ukraine, Amnesty International’s African section directors said in an open letter ahead of the summit, which takes place from 28 to 29 October in Moscow. “For African leaders to remain silent on this issue would be a profound disservice to the people of their countries. We urge them to address this issue directly with the Russian authorities at the Russia-Africa Summit 2026 and call on Russia to take immediate steps to end these practices, which in many cases amount to trafficking — a crime under international law,” said directors of Amnesty International’s sections across Africa. “At a moment when many African governments are speaking up about the enduring legacy of colonialism, and the importance of sovereignty and African agency in international affairs, they must reject any practice that treats nationals of African countries as a commodity for other countries’ political and military objectives.” For African leaders to remain silent on this issue would be a profound disservice to the people of their countries. We urge them to address this issue directly with the Russian authorities at the Russia-Africa Summit 2026 and call on Russia to take immediate steps to end these practices, which in many cases amount to trafficking — a crime under international law. Amnesty International’s Section Directors across Africa “African leaders must demand investigations and prosecutions for all acts of trafficking in persons involving state officials or others acting with the acquiescence of the Russian authorities.” At a moment when many African governments are speaking up about the enduring legacy of colonialism, and the importance of sovereignty and African agency in international affairs, they must reject any practice that treats nationals of African countries as a commodity for other countries’ political and military objectives. Amnesty International Section Directors across Africa Background In a briefing published 10 September 2026, “Russia: Trafficking of Foreign Nationals to Fight in Ukraine ” ,Amnesty International documented how the Russian authorities recruit people from African countries through deception, coercion and the exploitation of economic hardship amounting in many cases to trafficking, drawing them into devastating military combat, far from home, and often in circumstances which leave them little or no choice but to fight.

A new bill before Sri Lanka’s parliament that grants the authorities sweeping arbitrary powers to tackle ‘organized crime’ and deny suspects’ human rights should be immediately withdrawn, Amnesty International said today. The Prevention of Organised Crimes bill, tabled in Sri Lanka’s parliament on 6 October, contains provisions that would make confessions extracted under duress admissible in court, enable the detention of suspects for up to two years without trial, and ban the media from reporting on court proceedings. The bill also confers the police with wide powers to conduct searches without a warrant, and imprison people for not providing information to authorities. The bill mirrors many elements of Sri Lanka’s repressive Prevention of Terrorism Act (PTA), which has been misused since the 1970s to target minorities and repress dissent. “This extraordinary bill is the most alarming in a string of repressive laws proposed by the National People’s Power (NPP) government. It reintroduces most of the very worst elements of the PTA and applies them to a wide range of offences,” said Smriti Singh, Amnesty International’s South Asia Director. We urge the Sri Lankan government to withdraw the bill in its entirety Smriti Singh, Amnesty International’s South Asia Director “The bill entrenches impunity and risks reviving the conditions that enabled arbitrary detention, torture and other ill-treatment under the PTA, including the use of coerced statements to secure convictions. It allows what effectively amounts to secret trials and it removes virtually all the safeguards designed to prevent the abuse of police power. The international community, which saw and decried the abuses under the PTA, should shudder. “We urge the Sri Lankan government to withdraw the bill in its entirety and engage in meaningful public consultations around how to tackle organized crime while protecting human rights.” The bill also empowers police to obtain personal information from telecommunications, satellite, digital and data service providers – including subscriber identities, call records and device location data – without a court order. This would infringe on the right to privacy and create significant risks of abuse, including the surveillance of journalists’ contacts, lawyers’ communications, and organizers of lawful assemblies. The bill covers offences already criminalized under Sri Lankan law, including intellectual property violations, Penal Code offences such as obstructing public servants and secret wrongful confinement, but subjects them to fewer due process safeguards when committed by an organized criminal group, to support prosecutions. An organized criminal group is defined in the bill as “a structured group of three or more persons, existing for a period of time and acting in concert... in order to obtain, directly or indirectly, a financial or other material benefit”. To determine whether an individual is a member of such a group, courts are allowed to consider a range of circumstantial evidence including their “style of dress, hand signs, language or tattoos used by known members of the organised criminal group” or whether they visit places known to be used by organized criminal groups. Courts are also allowed to consider past conduct and association as admissible evidence to prove membership of an organized criminal group. Statements made before a magistrate by persons who can’t be cross-examined – on account of their being dead or because they cannot be found – are also permitted as evidence of criminal conduct, while a provision in the bill making it an offence to knowingly do “any other act... in furtherance of a common criminal object borne by the members of an organised criminal group” is extremely vague, and subject to possible abuse. “Criminal guilt must be based on actual evidence of individual wrongdoing from objective factual circumstances defined by law with sufficient precision, not appearance, association or suspicion. Provisions that allow people to be branded members of criminal groups based on how they dress, whom they know or where they go risk discriminatory profiling and undermine the prohibition of arbitrary detention and the right to a fair trial,” said Smriti Singh. Criminal guilt must be based on actual evidence of individual wrongdoing Smriti Singh The proposed bill risks facilitating torture and other ill-treatment by weakening key safeguards against coercion and undermining fair trial guarantees. By making confessions to police officers above the rank of Assistant Superintendent admissible evidence and removing protections against torture and other ill-treatment, it increases the risk that coerced confessions could be used to secure convictions. The bill also reverses the burden of proof in relation to torture and other ill-treatment, with the onus placed on accused persons to prove that abuse occurred. Judges are permitted to alter indictments mid-trial from organized crime offences to ordinary offences when there is no evidence of the former, instead of discharging the suspect and the prosecution filing a new indictment for the correct offence. These provisions further undermine fair trial rights, due process and safeguards against arbitrary detention and risk reproducing features of the PTA, creating conditions conducive to torture or other ill-treatment and impunity for perpetrators. Under its provisions, an individual accused of being a member of an organized criminal group can be detained for up to a year before being charged and for a further year in pretrial detention. It also creates a legal obligation to give information to police, including information that would otherwise be protected by privilege, with punishments of up to seven years in prison and/or a fine of up to 200,000 rupees (approximately 600 USD) for failing to do so. “Sri Lanka is following a dangerous path by introducing legislation that weakens safeguards against torture and other ill-treatment and that puts fair trial guarantees at risk, repeating the mistakes of the PTA. This must stop. Allowing statements that could have been obtained by torture or other ill-treatment to be admissible in court while shifting the burden onto victims to prove their abuse risks entrenching impunity and undermining the fundamental rights of anyone accused of a crime,” said Smriti Singh. Background The National People’s Power government recently passed into law amendments to the Financial Transactions Reporting Act, the Convention on the Suppression of Terrorist Financing Act, and the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, which civil society organizations have criticized for undermining the rights to freedom of association and expression. The government is currently in the process of repealing the draconian Prevention of Terrorism Act by attempting to replace it with the proposed Protection of the State from Terrorism Act, which Amnesty International has also raised alarm over.

https://www.omct.org/en/resources/urgent.body: Share KEN 003 / 1126 / OBS 056 Abduction / Enforced disappearance / Transnational repression / Risk of arbitrary detention Kenya/Tanzania 2 November 2026 The Observatory for the Protection of Human Rights Defenders, a partnership of the International Federation for Human Rights (FIDH) and the World Organisation Against Torture (OMCT),requests your urgent intervention in the following situation in Tanzania and Kenya . Description of the situation: The Observatory has been informed about the abduction and enforced disappearance amid concerns of acts of transnational repression of Mr Twaha Mwaipaya , a Tanzanian human rights defender and former youth leader of the opposition party Chama cha Demokrasia na Maendeleo (CHADEMA). Through his public advocacy, Mr Mwaipaya has mobilised for democracy, justice, human rights, civic freedoms and accountability in Tanzania, and has denounced government repression, arbitrary detention and enforced disappearances. On 25 October 2026, at approximately 2:00 p.m., unidentified individuals travelling in three vehicles intercepted Mr Mwaipaya and abducted him while he was travelling by taxi with a friend to Kamulu, Machakos County, in Kenya, where he lives legally in exile since 2025. According to testimonies, a vehicle blocked their way and masked men prevented the doors from being opened. While his friend managed to escape, the abductors forced the taxi driver to drive away with Mr Mwaipaya still inside. At the time of publication of this Urgent Appeal, Mr Mwaipaya’s whereabouts remain unknown, the identities of those responsible have not yet been established, and no investigation on his abduction has been opened. His abduction has been reported to the Kenyan Police and an habeas corpus has been filed on 28 October 2026. The Observatory recalls that Mr Mwaipaya has faced repeated acts of harassment, threats, arbitrary arrests and detention in connection with his activism in the past in Tanzania. One such incident occurred on 30 June 2022, when he was arrested by the police in Morogoro while travelling from Dodoma to Dar es Salaam, over statements he had made online. His family and lawyers initially faced difficulties establishing where he was being held, prompting CHADEMA to file a habeas corpus application before the High Court of Tanzania. He was released on police bail after approximately five days in custody. In September 2023, he was reportedly arrested again after police prevented CHADEMA members from entering Ngorongoro for a scheduled political rally. In April 2025, Mr Mwaipaya and eight colleagues were arrested after attending court proceedings in the treason case against Mr Tundu Lissu, a lawyer and former president of CHADEMA. They were taken to a wooded area in Ununio, where they were tortured, before being abandoned in the Pande wildlife area in Bagamoyo. He reported extensive bruising across his body and difficulty sitting down. Following the violence surrounding Tanzania’s general elections on 29 October 2025 , Mr Mwaipaya continued to denounce alleged abuses by government authorities and police, including violations affecting opposition members and young people. From September 2025 onwards, uniformed police officers repeatedly visited his home while searching for him, threatening his relatives and neighbours. Before leaving Tanzania, he was threatened with being “disappeared” permanently, with reference to the case of Mr Deusdedith Soka, who was abducted in 2024 and remains missing. Due to these threats and continued surveillance, Mr Mwaipaya had to move to Kenya in 2025, where he continued his public advocacy while living in exile. His unlawful abduction in Kenya, where he is legally living, does not only contravene various provisions of Kenya's Constitution but also Article 104 of the Treaty for the Establishment of the East African Community, which establishes free movement of persons, labour, services, and the right of establishment and residence between the signatory states, including Tanzania and Kenya. His abduction in Kenya raises serious concerns about possible transnational repression, particularly given the threats he reportedly received in Tanzania before leaving the country and the continued targeting of human rights defenders and political activists beyond their country of origin in the region. This abduction and enforced disappearance have happened in a context where an increasing number of acts of transnational repression in East Africa has been documented by the Observatory in 2025 and 2026, with an established collaboration between Tanzania and Kenya. The Observatory is gravely concerned about the abduction and enforced disappearance of Twaha Mwaipaya and the risk that he may be subjected to arbitrary detention, ill-treatment or other serious human rights violations linked to his human rights work and activism in Tanzania. The Observatory calls for an investigation into all possible leads, including any potential cross-border links, and urges the Kenyan authorities to ensure that he is not forcibly returned to Tanzania, where he has previously faced threats and persecution. The Observatory urges the Kenyan authorities to take all necessary measures to immediately establish Mr Mwaipaya’s whereabouts, ensure his safety and physical and psychological integrity, and investigate the circumstances of his abduction. The Observatory also calls on the Tanzanian authorities to refrain from any action that could endanger him and to ensure that he is not subjected to reprisals for his legitimate human rights work. Actions requested: Please write to the authorities of Kenya asking them to: Immediately establish the whereabouts of Twaha Mwaipaya and ensure his safety and physical and psychological integrity; Launch an independent, impartial and effective investigation into Twaha Mwaipaya’s abduction, including any potential links to his human rights work and political activism in Tanzania and any possible involvement of actors operating across borders, as well as previous acts of harassment that may constitute transnational repression, and bring those responsible to justice; Ensure that Twaha Mwaipaya is protected from torture, ill-treatment, enforced disappearance and any other human rights violations, and that he is not forcibly returned to Tanzania in violation of the principle of non-refoulement; Take effective measures to prevent acts of transnational repression against human rights defenders and political activists seeking refuge in Kenya; Guarantee that human rights defenders and individuals seeking refuge in Kenya can exercise their legitimate activities without fear of abduction, intimidation or reprisals. Please also write to the Tanzanian authorities , urging them to: Refrain from any action that could endanger Twaha Mwaipaya or expose him to reprisals in connection with his human rights work; Take all necessary measures to help establish the whereabouts of Twaha Mwaipaya and ensure his safety; End all forms of harassment and intimidation against human rights defenders and their families, and guarantee that they can carry out their legitimate activities without fear of reprisals. https://www.fidh.org/en/en/international.body: 02/11/2026 Press release European Court of Human Rights Italy International Criminal Court (ICC) Libya FIDH In a third-party intervention, the International Federation for Human Rights (FIDH) argues that the International Criminal Court’s (ICC) finding of Italy’s non-compliance with the Rome Statute and the ongoing non-cooperation procedure before the Assembly of States Parties, should not prevent the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) from examining individual applications alleging human rights violations arising from Italy’s failure to surrender a Libyan suspect to the ICC. FIDH stresses that victims must not be denied the opportunity to seek redress before the ECtHR and calls for recognition of the distinct but complementary obligations of states to cooperate with international criminal justice mechanisms and to protect individual human rights. In a separate third-party intervention in the same proceedings, REDRESS , Route Justice and TRIAL International address the scope of states’ procedural obligations under Articles 2 and 3 of the Convention in relation to serious international crimes committed abroad, arguing that where certain jurisdictional criteria are met, such obligations require meaningful cooperation with the ICC to secure accountability. Paris, 2 November 2026. On 30 October, the International Federation for Human Rights (FIDH) filed a third-party intervention before the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) in support of two applications against Italy ( Y v. Italy ] and Z v. Italy ]) concerning its failure to surrender Osama Elmasry Njeem to the ICC in January 2025, despite an ICC arrest warrant. FIDH stresses that proceedings against a state for non-cooperation with the ICC do not make individual human rights complaints against that state inadmissible before the ECtHR . The two applications raise distinct questions about Italy’s obligations to protect individual rights under the European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR), including the right to an effective investigation and access to a court. FIDH’s intervention explains why the ICC non-cooperation procedure, which includes both the non-compliance proceeding at the ICC and the ongoing referral before the Assembly of States Parties (ASP), does not preclude the ECtHR from examining these alleged human rights violations. The applicants allege that Italy’s failure to surrender Mr Njeem, alongside other alleged failures, has undermined their ability to obtain accountability for serious abuses they suffered in Libya. The cases also highlight a fundamental challenge to international justice: the ICC depends on states to execute its arrest warrants, and failure to cooperate can undermine accountability for the gravest international crimes . States Parties to the Rome Statute, including Italy, must uphold their cooperation obligations. When a state fails to do so, the consequences extend beyond its relationship with the Court, potentially depriving victims of meaningful opportunities to obtain justice and redress. At a time when the ICC faces growing political pressure and challenges to states’ cooperation, this case underscores the importance of upholding the Rome Statute’s cooperation framework. The stakes are particularly high in Libya, where accountability for serious international crimes remains essential . Mr Njeem is suspected of serious crimes allegedly committed at Mitiga Prison, including murder, torture, rape and other sexual violence. FIDH and its partners have separately documented the abuses of migrants and refugees in Libya, amounting to crimes against humanity, and called for accountability through a joint report and an A rticle 15 communication to the ICC . " States cannot treat cooperation with the ICC as a merely procedural obligation. When a state fails to execute an arrest warrant, it risks undermining the pursuit of justice for victims of the gravest crimes. The ECtHR must be able to examine whether that failure also violates individual rights protected by the Convention, and ensure that victims are not left without an effective avenue for redress ," said Alexis Deswaef, FIDH President . By intervening in these proceedings, FIDH seeks to ensure that the ICC non-cooperation procedure is understood as a distinct but complementary mechanism from the protection of individual rights under the ECHR. The case offers the ECtHR an important opportunity to clarify the relationship between states’ obligations to cooperate with international criminal justice and their responsibility to guarantee effective human rights protection. Background – The ICC case On 18 January 2025, the ICC issued an arrest warrant for Mr Njeem in connection with the situation in Libya . He is suspected of crimes against humanity and war crimes, including murder, torture, rape and other sexual violence, allegedly committed in Libya from February 2015 onwards, including at Mitiga Prison. Italian authorities arrested Mr Njeem in Turin on 19 January 2025 but returned him to Libya two days later, despite the ICC’s request for cooperation. On 17 October 2025, the ICC found that Italy had failed to comply with its obligations under the Rome Statute by failing to execute the request to arrest and surrender Mr Njeem. On 29 January 2026, the ICC Presidency referred Italy’s non-compliance to the Assembly of States Parties. – The ECtHR applications and FIDH’s intervention Two applications have been lodged against Italy before the ECtHR. Applicant Y %7D]., whose application was lodged on 16 April 2025, alleges violations of Articles 2 and 3 of the ECHR, concerning the right to life and the prohibition of torture, in connection with Italy’s alleged failure to fulfil its procedural obligations to investigate serious violations and ensure accountability. He also argues that these obligations may require cooperation with foreign or international authorities in transnational cases. Applicant Z %7D]., whose application was lodged on 7 February 2026, alleges, among other matters, a violation of Article 6 § 1, concerning the right of access to a court, as well as failures to address alleged violations of fundamental rights, including the prohibitions of torture, slavery and forced labour. FIDH’s third-party intervention addresses the admissibility of these applications under Article 35 § 2(b) of the Convention. It argues that the applications are not substantially the same as the ICC’s non-cooperation procedure because they involve different parties and complaints. It further argues that the ICC’s non-cooperation procedure does not constitute another procedure of international investigation or settlement that would bar the ECtHR from examining the applicants’ claims, as it is not capable of providing individual victims with effective protection or redress. The intervention therefore highlights a key distinction: the non-cooperation procedure concerns Italy’s Rome Statute obligations towards the ICC, whereas proceedings before the ECtHR allow individuals to seek justice and redress for alleged violations of their Convention rights. – Complementary third-party intervention In a separate third-party intervention in the same proceedings, REDRESS , Route Justice and TRIAL International address the scope of states’ procedural obligations under Articles 2 and 3 of the Convention in relation to serious international crimes committed abroad. They argue that a State’s procedural obligations under Articles 2 and 3 of the European Convention on Human Rights extends to securing accountability for torture, crimes against humanity, and war crimes committed abroad where a suspect is present on its territory. The brief submits that the suspect’s presence, a competent international court’s request for arrest and surrender, relevant international obligations to investigate or prosecute, and the absence of realistic alternative avenues for accountability can together establish the necessary jurisdictional link under Article 1. https://www.fidh.org/en/en/region/north-.body: 03/11/2026 Press release Lebanon ar en fr Israel & Palestine France National courts Ali Cherri Six months after the complaint was filed in France by the Franco-Lebanese artist Ali Cherri and the International Federation for Human Rights (FIDH), a judicial investigation has been opened by the French War Crimes Unit. This investigation aims to shed light on the Israeli army’s bombing of a residential building in Beirut on 26 November 2024, which killed seven civilians, including the artist’s parents. To FIDH’s knowledge, this is the first judicial investigation into the crimes committed by the Israeli army in Lebanon since the start of the military operation in October 2023. Paris, 3 November 2026. Following the complaint filed in France on 1 April 2026 by the Franco-Lebanese artist and filmmaker Ali Cherri, alongside the International Federation for Human Rights (FIDH), a judicial investigation has been opened on charges of intentionally directing an attack against a civilian object, amounting to a war crime. Two investigating judges from the French War Crimes Unit have been appointed to investigate the case. On 26 November 2024, just a few hours before the ceasefire agreement between Israel and Hezbollah was due to come into effect, Ali Cherri’s family appartment was targeted by an Israeli military bombing, killing seven people, including the artist’s parents, Mahmoud Naim Cherri and Nadira Hayek, as well as a domestic worker employed by the couple, Birki Negesa. Located in the residential neighborhood of Noueiri in Beirut (Lebanon), the building targeted by the strikes housed Ali Cherri’s apartment on the 9th floor, where his parents lived. The bombing completely destroyed this apartment, as well as those on the 7th and 8th floors of the building. " The opening of this judicial investigation marks another important step in our fight against impunity and our struggle for justice for those who were killed. For my family and me, it is essential that this investigation establish responsibility, and ensure that those who ordered and carried out this bombing are held accountable for their actions, " says Ali Cherri . " To our knowledge, this is the very first judicial investigation opened into the crimes committed by the Israeli army in Lebanon since October 2023, " says Clémence Bectarte, lawyer and coordinator of the FIDH Litigation Action Group . " We hope that this investigation will shed full light on the bombing of 26 November 2024, which we qualified as a war crime in our complaint. " As Ali Cherri holds dual French and Lebanese nationality, the judicial investigation will focus only on the bombing of his apartment. Indeed, the French courts do not have jurisdiction over the events that led to the deaths of the victims, who were not French nationals. Ақтөбе облысы. Ырғыз-Торғай резерваты қорындағы сурет. БҰҰ-ның Азық-түлік және ауыл шаруашылығы ұйымы (FAO), Қоршаған орта бағдарламасы (UNEP) және Биологиялық алуан түрлілік туралы конвенция хатшылығы дайындаған жаңа есепте Қазақстанның табиғат экожүйелерін қалпына келтіру жөніндегі екі бағыты аталды. Римде жарияланған "Табиғаттың оралуы: экожүйелерді қалпына келтіруді адамның және ғаламшардың игілігіне пайдалану" (Nature’s comeback: Scaling ecosystem restoration for people and planet) атты құжат — "БҰҰ-ның экожүйелерді қалпына келтіру онжылдығы (2021–2030)" аясындағы жетістіктерді бағалайтын есеп. Есепке сәйкес, 2026 жылы бүкіл әлемде шамамен 252 млн гектар жерде экожүйені қалпына келтіру процесі жүрген. Авторлар мұны "тарихтағы ең ауқымды қалпына келтіру әрекеті" деп сипаттайды. Сонымен бірге құжатта әлем "белгіленген межеге жету жоспарынан артта келе жатқаны", ал қабылданған міндеттемелерді 2030 жылға дейін орындау үшін "қарқынды үш есе арттыру қажеттігі" ескертіледі. Қазақстанның "Алтын дала" бастамасы есепте БҰҰ бойынша таңдап алынған 35 "Әлемдік қалпына келтіру эталон жобасының" (UN World Restoration Flagships) қатарында аталады. Есепте бұл жобалар "үлкен мақсаттары, ауқымы және басқа жерлерде қайталануы мүмкіндігі үшін таңдалған, үкімет қолдаған бастамалар" деп сипатталған. Барлық 35 жоба бірге 18 млн гектар жерді қамтып, 1 миллионнан астам "жасыл" жұмыс орнын ашуы тиіс. Құжат жануарлар популяциясын қалпына келтірудің нақты мысалдарын айтқанда Қазақстанды бөлек атайды. Есепте бұл жобалардың нәтижесінде "Шығыс Африкадағы тау горилласы, Бразилияның Атлантика орманындағы ягуар мен маймыл, Қырғызстандағы қар барысы, Үндістандағы Ганг өзені дельфиндерінің, сондай-ақ Қазақстан даласындағы киік пен керқұланның оралғаны" айтылады. "Алтын Дала" бастамасы – 2006 жылы Қазақстан үкіметі мен бірқатар табиғат қорғау ұйымдары серіктесіп іске асыра бастаған үлкен жоба. Мақсаты – Қазақстанның мыңдаған шақырым сулы-батпақты және шөлейт экожүйесін қорғап, ондағы жабайы табиғатты қалпына келтіру. Ресми есеп бойынша, киік саны 2003 жылғы 20 мыңнан 2024 жылы 2,8 миллионға өскен. Азаттық бұл өсім шаруашылықтарға қиындық туғызып, шаруаларға шығын келтіргені туралы да жазған. Киік саны артуына байланысты Қазақстан үкіметі оның санын реттеу мақсатында атуға квота белгілеген. Бұған қарсылар да көп болған. Есептегі екінші дерек тұщы су экожүйесін қалпына келтіруге қатысты. Құжатқа сенсек, Қазақстан осы бағыт бойынша ең көп ауданды қамтитын елдер қатарында алтыншы орында тұр. Қазақстан 0,33 млн гектар тұщы су экожүйесін қалпына келтіру процесінде деп көрсеткен — бұл елдің жалпы жер аумағының шамамен 0,1 пайызы. Салыстыру үшін алсақ, бұл көрсеткіш бойынша Индонезия (5,99 млн га), Польша (0,97 млн га), Бенин (0,93 млн га), Камерун (0,60 млн га) және Ирак (0,40 млн га) тұр. Қазақстаннан кейін АҚШ (0,31 млн га), Нидерланд (0,27 млн га), Кения (0,21 млн га) және Моңғолия (0,16 млн га) тұр. Жалпы алғанда, әлемде 62 елде шамамен 11 млн гектар тұщы су экожүйесі қалпына келтіріліп жатыр. Есеп авторлары бұл деректі елдердің табиғатты "қалпына келтіру тиімділігінің рейтингі ретінде түсіндірілмеуі керегін", ал пайыздық көрсеткіштер табиғатты қалпына келтіру "тиімділігінің өлшемі емес" екенін де ескетеді. Авторлар пайымынша, әр елдің жер аумағына, қалпына келтіру бағдарламасының ауқымына, сондай-ақ мониторинг пен есеп беру деңгейіне де байланысты айырмашылық болуы мүмкін. Құжатта жалпы тұщы су мен теңіз және жағалау экожүйелерін қалпына келтіру "межеленген мақсаттардан әлдеқайда артта қалып отырғаны", ал дәл осы экожүйелер "өте жоғары қарқынмен тозып жатқаны" да ескертіледі. Қазақстан мұнайын Ресей арқылы халықаралық нарыққа шығаратын бұл құбыр 2 қарашаға қараған түні "Самара" өндірістік-диспетчерлік станциясына жасалған дрон шабуылынан соң өз жұмысын тоқтатқан. Қазақстан энергетика министрлігінің мәлімдеуінше, техникалық тексерістен соң құбыр жұмысы қалыпты режимде қайта іске қосылған. Кейінгі жылы Украина Ресейдегі энергетика инфрақұрылымына тұрақты түрде шабуылдап келеді. Оның ішінде Қазақстан мұнайын Еуропа нарығына жеткізетін Каспий құбыр консорциумының нысандары да бар. КҚК инфрақұрылымына шабуыл Қазақстан билігінің наразылығын тудырған. Құбыр арқылы АҚШ мұнай компаниялары өндірген шикізат та тасымалданатындықтан, Вашингтон Киевке КҚК-ға соққы жасамауды сұраған. Ресей де Украина энергетика нысандарына шабуыл жасап келеді. Украина мониторинг арналарының мәліметінше, "Самара" өндірістік-диспетчерлік станциясынан өрт шыққан . Ал Reuters агенттігінің сауда саласындағы дерек көзі мұнай тасымалы 2 қарашаның кешінде қайта іске қосылуы мүмкін деген. ДНҚ-талдау туыстығын растаған 3 қараша 2026 жыл, 14:17 Наташа Қалымбетова көз жазып қалған қызымен АҚШ-та қауышты. ДНҚ-талдау туыстығын растаған Бөлісу Сілтемесін көшіру Facebook X (Twitter) WhatsApp Email Бөлісу Бөлісу Сілтемесін көшіру Facebook X (Twitter) WhatsApp Email Бөлісу PDF VPN-сіз оқу Сайт бұғатталып тұрса да, материалды осы сілтемемен кіріп оқуға болады Google-да басымдық бер Наташа Қалымбетова 1990 жылдардың ортасында жыныстық зорлық салдарынан жүкті болып, туыстарын қолдау таппай сәбиін бөбектер үйіне берген, артынан одан көз жазып қалған Наташа Қалымбетова АҚШ-та қызымен қауышты. ДНҚ-талдау олардың туыс екенін растады. Бұл туралы Қалымбетованың өзі мәлімдеді. "Ұзақ күткен жаңалық. Нәтиже шықты. Міне қараңыздар: 99,999999 пайыз. Айттым ғой, ол менің қызым деп. Оны көргенде бірден түсіндім. Бірақ ол қобалжыды. Оның қолында менің құжаттарым бола тұра, америкалық болған соң ДНҚ нәтижесін көргісі келді. Міне құжат шықты, ол менің қызым" деді ол TikTok желісінде жариялаған видеосында. Наташа Қалымбетова биыл көктемде өз басынан өткен оқиғаны айтып, Қазақстанда резонанс тудырған. Өзінің айтуынша, 1994 жылы 17 жасында Батыс Қазақстан облысында төрт жігіт оны зорлап, салдарынан аяғы ауыр болып қалған. Қалымбетова бұл мәлімдемені жасағанда Таиландта тұратынын айтқан. Оның сөзі қызу талқы тудырған тұста БҚО полициясы 32 жыл бұрынғы оқиға бойынша қылмыстық іс қозғап, Қалымбетова куәлік беруге елге шақырған. Жаздың басында зорлық оқиғасынан кейін Қалымбетова аяғы ауыр болып қалғанын, сәби дүниеге келген соң, туыстарынан қолдау болмай оны бөбектер үйіне өткізуге мәжбүр болғанын айтқан. ОҚИ ОТЫРЫҢЫЗ Зорланғанын 30 жылдан соң жариялаған Наташаның оқиғасы Бөбектер үйіне үш жыл бойы барып жүргенін айтқан Қалымбетова араға уақыт салып оралғанда америкалық отбасы оның қызын асырап алып, АҚШ-қа әкеткенін білген. Осы оқиғадан соң жеке деректері Қалымбетова айтқан жайттармен сәйкес келетін америкалық азаматша табылған. Бірақ Қалымбетова оның жеке өміріне нұқсан келеді деп қыздың аты-жөнін және суретін жарияламаған. Қызы шетелде жасалған ДНҚ-талдауға сеніңкіремей, талдауда АҚШ-та жасатқысы келген. Қазанның аяғында Қалымбетова АҚШ-қа барып, қызымен қауышқан соң, ДНҚ-талдауын жасатқан. Биыл шілдеде Қалымбетова Қазақстан президенті Қасым-Жомарт Тоқаевқа үндеу жасап, тергеудің алға жылжымай тұрғанын айтқан . Енді ол ДНҚ-талдаудың нәтижелері істі аяғына дейін жеткізуге көмектеседі деп үміттенеді. Наташа Қалымбетова көз жазып қалған қызымен АҚШ-та қауышты. Қылмыстық кодекстің 380-3 бабы бойынша, күш қолдану қаупін төндірген адамға 200-500 АЕК айыппұл, не сол мөлшерде түзеу жұмыстары, не 300 сағатқа дейін қоғамдық жұмысқа тарту, не екі жылға дейін бас бостандығын шектеу не сол мерзімге бас бостандығынан айыру жазасы қарастырылған.
