https://tass.com/politics/2210737.body: Ukraine crisis Human rights ombudswoman comments on convoy heading to Alyoshki, security arrangements According to Yana Lantratova, the ceasefire, announced in connection with a humanitarian mission in the town of Alyoshki in the Kherson Region, is being respected Russian Human Rights Commissioner Yana Lantratova © TASS MOSCOW, October 30. /TASS/. The humanitarian convoy organized for residents of the town of Alyoshki in Kherson Region comprises 25 buses, Russian Human Rights Commissioner Yana Lantratova told reporters. She also said that a sapper and another person were killed while conducting mine clearance along the routes to ensure the safe passage of the humanitarian mission. TASS has summarized the key statements made by Russia’s Human Rights Commissioner. Ceasefire compliance The ceasefire, announced in connection with a humanitarian mission in the town of Alyoshki in the Kherson Region, is being respected: "The ceasefire in the humanitarian mission zone in Alyoshki is holding. There have been no incidents reported. The Russian and Ukrainian sides are fully meeting their commitments." Mine clearance operations in Alyoshki Two people, including a sapper, were killed while conducting mine clearance operations along the routes to guarantee the safe passage of the humanitarian mission: "A sapper was killed during mine clearance, and another person also died. We extend our condolences to the families and relatives of those who lost their lives." Russian military personnel have finished clearing mines along the routes designated for the humanitarian mission in Alyoshki: "Mine clearance along the routes for the humanitarian mission in Alyoshki has been completed. We thank our military personnel, who put their lives at risk to prepare the roads for safe passage." Residents prepared to evacuate The convoy carrying aid will proceed to the central district hospital: "The convoy will head to the central district hospital." Residents who have decided to leave Alyoshki will be able to do so until 2:00 p.m. Moscow time, with security measures being implemented: "Residents who have decided to leave the town will be allowed to do so until 2:00 p.m. All necessary security measures will be implemented. We plan to begin handing out humanitarian aid after 2:30 p.m." The humanitarian convoy comprises 25 buses: "A large convoy of 25 buses has been assembled for today. They can carry at least 750 people." Special buses for bedridden residents and ambulances are on standby to evacuate people from Alyoshki: "Special buses for bedridden people have been prepared in case they are needed. We have set aside around 30 places for them, as well as nine additional ambulances." A separate bus will be provided for people traveling with their pets as part of the humanitarian mission: "People said they wanted to take their pets with them. We discussed and made arrangements for this as well, so a separate bus will be provided <...> for those who want to take their pets with them." Journalists' coverage Journalists covering the humanitarian mission in Alyoshki will be able to meet and talk to residents in person: "Journalists are also working on site and will be able to speak with residents in person." More than 50 journalists from various countries have come to Kherson Region to report on the humanitarian mission: "Ukrainian journalists, American journalists, journalists from various countries - there are a great many of them, more than 50, so everything is happening openly. This is very important.". https://vlast.kz/novosti/71427-pravitels.body: фото Данияра Мусирова Твитнуть Поделиться Поделиться Поделиться Поделиться Поделиться Тамара Вааль, Астана, Власть Заместитель премьер-министра – министр национальной экономики Серик Жумангарин, рассмотрев депутатский запрос партии «Ак жол» по вопросу установления единой ставки 2-3 % по специальному налоговому режиму на основе упрощенной декларации заявил, что он требует дополнительной оценки. Как напомнил вице-премьер, по новому Налоговому кодексу базовая ставка по специальному налоговому режиму на основе упрощенной декларации составляет 4%. При этом маслихаты имеют право изменять ее и устанавливать в размере от 2 до 6%. В частности, в 2026 году маслихаты Астаны, Алматы, Актобе, Павлодара, Петропавловска и Уральска установили ставку на уровне 3%, а в Шымкенте, Караганде, Атырау, Кызылорде, Таразе, Талдыкоргане, Туркестане, Усть-Каменогорске, Семее и Конаеве – 2%. «Таким образом, действующий механизм уже позволяет устанавливать ставки ниже базового уровня. Вместе с тем вопрос введения единой ставки 2-3% по всей территории страны требует дополнительной оценки с точки зрения влияния на условия ведения бизнеса, доходы местных бюджетов и эффективность действующей модели», - говорится в ответе. Он добавил, что введение единой ставки на республиканском уровне и исключение полномочий маслихатов ограничит учет региональной специфики. А установление ставки 2-3% потребует расчетов бюджетных последствий и оценки изменения налоговой нагрузки для различных категорий предпринимателей. В Миннацэкономики считают целесообразным продолжить мониторинг применения СНР и провести анализ влияния региональной дифференциации ставок на деятельность субъектов МСБ и только по итогам «может быть рассмотрен вопрос о внесении соответствующих изменений». «Таким образом, на данном этапе предложение об установлении единой ставки СНР на основе упрощенной декларации в размере 2–3% по всей территории Республики Казахстан и исключении полномочий маслихатов по ее корректировке не поддерживается», - написал вице-премьер, подчеркнув, что вопрос по совершенствованию действующего механизма стоит рассматривать «по результатам комплексного анализа его практического применения». При этом Жумангарин указывает, что «риска миграции бизнеса между регионами из-за различий в ставках на текущем этапе нет». По его словам, в целом механизм региональной дифференциации не является новым, так как до 2026 года аналогичный подход применялся в рамках специального налогового режима розничного налога. Например, в 2024 году в Алматы сохранялась базовая ставка 4%, в Астане – 3%, в Карагандинской области – 2%, однако, утверждает вице-премьер, «массового перетока бизнеса из Алматы в регионы с более низкой ставкой не фиксировалось». «С 1 января 2026 года принцип региональной дифференциации сохранен в рамках СНР на основе упрощенной декларации и к настоящему времени применяется девять месяцев. При ставке 3% в Астане и 2% в Карагандинской области признаков массовой перерегистрации бизнеса не наблюдается. Это подтверждается и фактическими показателями: по данным формы 910.00 за первое полугодие 2026 года заявленный доход налогоплательщиков вырос в Астане на 23,2%, в Карагандинской области – на 23%, в Алматы – на 18,3%», - привел он статистику. Власть — это независимое медиа в Казахстане. Поддержите журналистику, которой доверяют. https://kaktus.media/doc/555777_vybory_p.body: kaktus.media Выборы президента. Насколько труден тест по кыргызскому языку. Реальный опыт Политика 2983 30 октября 2026 10:33 Kaktus Все самое интересное в Telegram В январе 2027 года в Кыргызстане пройдут выборы президента. Кандидаты обязательно должны пройти тест в "Кыргызтесте" на знание кыргызского языка на уровне не ниже В2. Для справки : уровень B2 ("пороговый продвинутый") - это четвертый уровень владения языком. Он позволяет свободно общаться, учиться и работать в кыргызскоязычной среде. Те, кто владеют языком на таком уровне, могут свободно и спонтанно поддерживать беседу с носителями языка, умеют аргументировать свою точку зрения и вести дискуссии. Распознают речь на слух даже при наличии акцента или на высокой скорости. Читайте также: Выборы президента. Коротко о самом главном (обновлено 28 октября) Илим Карыпбеков на сдаче "Кыргызтеста". Как оказалось, не все носители языка могут сдать экзамен с первого раза. Например, это не получилось у Омурбека Суваналиева и Сыймыка Жапыкеева , которые планировали выставить свои кандидатуры на предстоящих выборах. Жапыкеев решил пересдать: в итоге он набрал необходимые 63 балла. Как проходит тестирование на знание кыргызского языка? Илим Карыпбеков, экс-гендиректор КТРК, а ныне просто блогер (как сказал он сам), сдал тест и рассказал Kaktus.media , как это было. - Почему вы решили попробовать сдать тест? - Я просто решил узнать, насколько хорошо владею языком. Раньше я такой тест никогда не сдавал. Когда-то давно я проходил только TOEFL . Больше я тесты на знание языков не сдавал. Кыргызский язык, конечно, для меня родной, хотя до 9-го класса учился на русском языке. Но 10-й и 11-й классы я окончил на кыргызском. Приехав в Бишкек, понял, что здесь превалирует русский, но тем не менее кыргызский я не забывал. Всегда старался и стараюсь его продвигать. Интересный момент: многие носители языка думают, что они знают кыргызский хорошо, но это не всегда так, к сожалению. Есть разница в обычном, бытовом, языке и в литературной норме. И для работы на госслужбе, конечно, нужно знать хорошо именно литературный язык: для работы с документооборотом и в других сферах нужно владеть на продвинутом уровне. - Как проходила сама процедура сдачи теста? - Я позвонил и спросил про возможность сдать тест. На тестирование надо записываться заранее. Сам тест занимает около двух часов: по полчаса на каждый раздел. Там есть отсчет времени, что позволяет не забывать о времени. Сам тест сдается полностью онлайн. За сдачу четырех блоков - лексики, орфографии, аудирования и сочинения - заплатил 450 сомов. Это достаточно дешево, учитывая, что такая работа выполняется! Когда начал сдавать, понял, что для меня это достаточно легкий уровень. Я могу сдать не только президентский минимум (то есть B2), но и уровень выше - С1. Совсем скоро обещали внедрить проверку на уровень С2. Илим Карыпбеков на сдаче "Кыргызтеста". - То есть сложностей для вас не было? - Особых нет, но были технические особенности. Например, я допускал технические ошибки из-за отличительного интерфейса. На моем компьютере раскладка букв Ң, Ө и Ү отличается. И получилось, что я нечаянно нажал не на те клавиши, и вопрос пропускался. А это означало, что я не ответил на какой-то вопрос. Так что пару баллов я недобрал из-за этого. Всего я набрал 80, 96, 85 и 90 баллов за каждый из блоков соответственно при минимальных 60. При пересдаче мои баллы были бы выше, потому что теперь я уже знаком с интерфейсом. - Что представляют вопросы в тестировании? - Необходимо выбирать вариант ответа. Вопросы касались склонения слов, спряжения глаголов. Где-то было пропущено подлежащее, сказуемое, и надо было выбрать верный ответ. В разделе "аудирование" был небольшой рассказ, который надо было понять и по нему ответить на вопросы. Затем надо было составить связный рассказ. Нельзя посчитать от 1 до 10 или просто наговорить некие слова. А некоторые так и делают, оказывается! Некоторые даже поют. Два блока - на лексику и орфографию - проверяются автоматически, а вот аудирование и сочинение проверяют специалисты - нанятые эксперты кыргызского языка. Поэтому итоговый результат получаешь не сразу. Мне кажется, что здесь есть вариант для каких-то манипуляций, несмотря на то что задания на проверку отправляются анонимно. То есть эксперты не знают, кто сдавал тест. - Искусственный интеллект при сдаче теста не применяется? - На данный момент нет, но, как рассказали специалисты "Кыргызтеста", до конца года они собираются вводить искусственный интеллект и исключить полностью вот этих независимых экспертов, филологов. Искусственный интеллект будет проверять и сразу выводить результаты теста, и только в случае апелляции, когда ты не согласен с "мнением" искусственного интеллекта, комиссионно филологи будут рассматривать результаты. Я понимаю Жапыкеева, когда он сказал, что сомневается в результатах. Наверное, в таких случаях надо публиковать результаты открыто, чтобы была дискуссия и прозрачность в этом вопросе. Но вообще, чтобы завалить этот тест, надо быть абсолютным двоечником. Требуемый для кандидатов в президенты уровень В2 - это уровень знания выпускников школы должен быть. - Как выбирается тема аудирования и сочинения? - Система выдает ее рандомно. Мне для сочинения досталась тема "Благодарность". Да, действительно, здесь нужно использовать слова, которые могут не применяться в обычной жизни. То есть не находятся в активном словарном запасе. Меня также предупредили, что если я просто напишу несколько слов, то тест не будет считаться пройденным. Там необходим объем минимум 15-18 предложений. Илим Карыпбеков на сдаче "Кыргызтеста". - У кыргызского языка есть диалекты. Учитывается ли это при сдаче теста? - Да, говор и диалект считается ошибкой. Об этом меня тоже предупредили. Всякие присказки в речи будут считаться минусом, она должна быть чистой, без слов-паразитов: жатыр-батыр, уникта миякта, например. Есть слова не паразиты, но их говорят по-разному. Но надо использовать литературную норму. У меня был какой-то вопрос, связанный с автомашиной, автотранспортом. Вот я как раз сказал: "Я очень стараюсь говорить без добавления русских и вообще иностранных слов. А в тексте как раз упомянута автомашина, но я говорю "автоунаа". Мне сказали, что такой вариант, конечно, допускается. На месте работают два специалиста - технический, который покажет, что и как делать, а также филолог, у которого можно что-то уточнить, например, по синонимам. Но не просить ответа на вопросы. При тестировании нужно быть внимательным. Могут быть какие-то особенности в тестировании, которые могут ввести в заблуждение. Илим Карыпбеков на сдаче "Кыргызтеста". - Правильно ли обязательное тестирование на знание языка при поступлении на государственную и муниципальную службу? - Лично я согласен с таким решением, потому что давно пора вводить стандарты в документообороте, чтобы все понимали, чтобы все было унифицировано. Надо распространять именно литературный кыргызский язык. У нас многие политики, даже самого высокого ранга, допускают такие банальные ошибки, используют диалектные слова, а это все потом распространяется. Такие тесты используют и в других странах. Люди же сдают TOEFL, IELTS и так далее. Хочется, чтобы скорее внедрили в работу ИИ. Тем более что апелляция при получении результатов предусматривается. https://asiaplus.news/en/2026/10/30/taji.body: Share Mehrofarin Najibi , asia+ Categories Governance Tajikistan Format News Published 30.10.2026 16:54 Translations Eng Тоҷ Рус Tajikistan’s lower house of parliament, Majlisi Namoyandagon, has passed a new law aimed at protecting the independence of the country’s statistical authorities and preventing unlawful interference by government bodies and officials. The legislation also introduces electronic reporting, expands access to administrative data and establishes a unified national system of official statistics. The Majlisi Namoyandagon approved the law “On Official Statistics” on October 21, according to the parliamentary newspaper Sadoi Mardum . The government-sponsored legislation will replace the existing Law “On State Statistics,” adopted in January 2010. The new law consists of six chapters and 29 articles. Government interference in statistics to be prohibited One of the key provisions of the new law is a ban on unlawful interference by government bodies and officials in the professional activities of statistical authorities. Jamshed Nurmahmadzoda, director of the Agency for Statistics under the President of Tajikistan, told lawmakers that the provision is intended to safeguard the independence and impartiality of official statistics. He said statistical indicators must be calculated in accordance with scientific and professional standards, without outside influence. The legislation also establishes principles of objectivity, reliability, transparency, accessibility and confidentiality, while strengthening the protection of personal and corporate data. Why is “state statistics” being renamed “official statistics”? According to Nurmahmadzoda, the change reflects a broader reform of how statistical information is collected, processed and published in Tajikistan. While the previous legislation focused primarily on statistical authorities, the new law establishes a national system of official statistics covering all authorized institutions involved in producing and disseminating statistical data. For the first time, this system will formally include not only the Agency for Statistics but also ministries, government agencies, the National Bank of Tajikistan and other authorized bodies. The Agency for Statistics will remain responsible for coordinating the system, including statistical methodologies, reporting programs and the use of data sources. The changes are intended to eliminate duplication in data collection, reduce unnecessary expenses and ensure that statistical indicators produced by different government institutions are comparable. What will change for businesses? The new legislation is also expected to simplify statistical reporting for businesses and reduce their administrative burden. Nurmahmadzoda explained that statistical authorities will be able to obtain administrative data directly from ministries and government agencies rather than repeatedly requesting the same information from businesses. The law also introduces several changes to the reporting system: Statistical reports will be submitted electronically. Electronic signatures and digital data exchange between government institutions will be introduced. Statistical registers will be established to maintain information on enterprises and other reporting entities. Reporting requirements will be clarified, with greater accountability for submitting accurate data on time. According to the head of the Statistics Agency, these measures will streamline data collection and make statistical reporting more efficient. Bringing Tajikistan’s statistics closer to international standards The new law also strengthens the role of the Interdepartmental Council on Statistics, expanding the participation of ministries, government agencies and experts in coordinating statistical activities. Nurmahmadzoda said the reforms are intended to improve the comparability of Tajikistan’s statistical indicators with those of other countries and strengthen public confidence in official data. However, he emphasized that adopting the legislation is only the first step. Its implementation will require closer cooperation between government institutions, improvements in statistical methodologies, further development of digital infrastructure and additional training for statistical professionals. Why is the 2010 law being replaced? According to Nurmahmadzoda, the existing legislation no longer fully meets modern requirements. He cited the growth of the digital economy, the emergence of new data sources, expanding international cooperation and increasingly demanding international statistical standards as the main reasons for the reform. Lawmaker Husniya Ishoqi said the legislation had also been developed in response to recommendations from the United Nations Statistical Commission, Eurostat and the Statistical Committee of the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS). The new law was drafted under the project “Modernization of the National Statistics System in Tajikistan,” with contributions from Tajik and international experts, including Kazakhstan-based StatCentr. The lower house approved the legislation without questions or debate. The law must still be approved by the upper house of parliament, Majlisi Milli, and signed by the president before it can enter into force following official publication. Join us on social media!

https://www.trend.az/casia/kazakhstan/42.body: Home Central Asia Kazakhstan Kazakhstan harvests 24.3 million tons of grain in 2026 - ministry Kazakhstan News 30 October 2026 10:07 (UTC +04:00) Photo: Government of Kazakhstan Alyona Pavlenko Journalist, International Desk Read more BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 30. Kazakhstan harvested 24.3 million tonnes of grain in 2026, one of the country's highest harvests in the past 15 years, with larger volumes recorded in only two previous record years, according to Kazakhstan's Ministry of Agriculture. According to the ministry, grain quality was another important result of the 2026 harvest. Preliminary data show that around 72% of the soft wheat delivered to grain elevators meets third-class standards. Gluten content exceeded 28% in 48% of the samples tested. In Akmola region, third-class wheat accounted for 90%, while Hi-Pro wheat accounted for 70%, according to the ministry. These quality indicators create additional opportunities to use Kazakh grain for food production, develop processing and strengthen the competitiveness of domestic products in international markets. Kazakhstan has also recorded strong export performance. Over the past two marketing years, the country exported 15.5 million tonnes and 16 million tonnes of grain and flour in grain equivalent, respectively. These were record volumes for the years since Kazakhstan gained independence. According to Kazakhstan Temir Zholy, the country's national railway company, grain exports reached 1.657 million tonnes from September through October 19, 2026, up 9%. The volume of mineral fertilizers applied has nearly tripled over the past three years, reaching 1.8 million tonnes in 2025. In 2026, 2.1 million tonnes had been applied against a target of 2.3 million tonnes. The share of elite seeds reached 12%, creating conditions for further improvements in crop yields and agricultural product quality. More than 130,000 tractors, 29,000 combine harvesters, 17,000 reapers and around 130,000 other agricultural machines were used during the 2026 harvest campaign. The depreciation rate of Kazakhstan's agricultural machinery fleet declined from 85% in 2023 to 65% in 2025. The country plans to raise the machinery renewal rate to 8% in 2026. A concessional leasing program is also supporting the modernization of the sector. Since the program was launched, farmers have acquired more than 12,700 tractors and 2,340 combine harvesters. Machinery purchased through the program accounts for nearly 10% of Kazakhstan's total fleet of tractors and combine harvesters. Agricultural production in Azerbaijan exceeded 11 billion manat ($6.5 billion) in January-September 2026, Azerbaijan’s Minister of Agriculture, Majnun Mammadov, said during an event held at the ministry’s administrative building to mark November 1 – Agriculture Workers' Day on Friday, Trend ’s correspondent reports from the event. The minister noted that the development of agriculture in Azerbaijan is one of the key priorities of state policy. According to him, the agrarian reforms initiated by National Leader Heydar Aliyev laid a solid foundation for the development of this sector; currently, under the leadership of President of Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev, consistent measures are being implemented to modernize the agrarian sector, enhance its competitiveness, and strengthen food security. Mammadov pointed out that the state program for the development of the production and processing of agricultural, fisheries, and aquaculture products for the years 2026–2030 defines the primary directions for a new phase in the development of the agrarian sector. "Within the framework of this program, key objectives include increasing productivity, implementing modern irrigation technologies, ensuring the efficient use of land and water resources, and expanding production and processing capacities," he remarked. According to the minister, it is essential to continue coordinated efforts with state institutions, the private sector, farmers, and other partners to achieve the goals set out in the state program. He emphasized that improving the legal framework of the agricultural sector, including the adoption of new laws "On seed production" and "On fisheries," as well as the implementation of new approaches to state support mechanisms, serves to create a more favorable operating environment for farmers. Mammadov mentioned that in the first 9 months of 2026, the production of grain crops rose by 8.2% compared to the same period last year, with wheat yields rising to 36.3 centners. Meanwhile, the production of fruits and berries grew by 5%, reaching 842,600 tons. A positive trend was also observed in the export of agricultural and processed products. He added that, despite these results, factors such as climate change, limited water resources, and shifts in international markets necessitate the adoption of more agile and innovative approaches within the agricultural sector. "Digitalization, the implementation of modern technologies, and the integration of scientific knowledge into production must remain the key priorities for agricultural development," the minister explained. The minister also stressed the particular importance of restoring the agricultural potential of the liberated territories. According to him, the establishment of modern farms in Karabakh and East Zangezur, the development of production infrastructure, and the incorporation of land resources into economic circulation are creating new opportunities for the country. https://cpj.org/2026/10/iran-sentences-j.body: Share this: Share on Bluesky (Opens in new window) Bluesky Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Share on LinkedIn (Opens in new window) LinkedIn Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on WhatsApp (Opens in new window) WhatsApp Email a link to a friend (Opens in new window) Email New York, October 28, 2026—The Committee to Protect Journalists calls on Iranian authorities to overturn the convictions and immediately release journalists Artin Ghazanfari and Omid Faraghat . The two were sentenced to 26 and 10 years under Iran’s sweeping espionage law , which also criminalizes routine media activities. “Iranian authorities are using espionage and national security laws to punish journalists for their work, handing down prison sentences that could take decades of their lives,” said Sara Qudah, CPJ’s regional director. “These sentences send a chilling message to every journalist in Iran. Authorities must overturn both convictions, immediately release Artin Ghazanfari and Omid Faraghat, and ensure Ghazanfari receives the medical care he urgently needs.” Ghazanfari, a Bahá’í photojournalist held at Greater Tehran Prison, was sentenced by Branch 15 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Abolqasem Salavati, according to the Human Rights Activists News Agency (HRANA) , run by the U.S.-based organization Human Rights Activists in Iran. The verdict was communicated to him on October 26. HRANA reported on October 28 , citing a source close to Ghazanfari’s family, that he received 20 years for “media activities,” five years for “assembly and collusion,” and one year for “propaganda against the state.” The source noted that the judge used Iran’s law on severe espionage punishments to hand down the 20-year term, bypassing the first charge’s standard 10-year maximum sentence. If the verdict is upheld, the longest individual sentence of 20 years could be enforced. Ghazanfari was arrested at his home in Tehran on January 19, 2026. Security agents searched his home and workplace, and confiscated electronic devices, books, and professional equipment. HRANA reported that Ghazanfari suffers from heart failure, high blood pressure , and asthma. Despite prison doctors recommending specialized treatment outside the facility, the judge has reportedly refused to authorize his transfer to a hospital. In a separate case, Branch 2 of the Karaj Revolutionary Court sentenced journalist Omid Faraghat to 10 years and one day in prison and permanently barred him from government and public-sector employment for “media and propaganda activities by producing content and publishing false news online contrary to national security,” according to his cousin, Mohammed Faraghat, who confirmed the details to CPJ, and Mashgh-e Solh , an Iranian news website. IranWire , an independent news outlet covering Iran, reported on October 28, citing the Khabaraneh Telegram news channel run by journalist and former political prisoner Mehdi Mahmoudian , that Faraghat was sentenced under Article 4 of Iran’s 2025 law intensifying punishments for espionage and cooperation with Israel and hostile states . The law also criminalizes certain political, cultural, and media activities, including publishing information authorities deem contrary to national security. Mohammed Faraghat told CPJ that the sentence had not yet been enforced and that the family had challenged the ruling. He said the appeal deadline had been reduced from 20 days to 10 days under the legislation. Faraghat was arrested on June 29, 2026, after being summoned by security police in Karaj, west of Tehran, and has since been held at Karaj Central Prison. He was initially accused of “disturbing public opinion” and “acting against national security.” CPJ emailed Iran’s mission to the United Nations in New York requesting comment but did not receive a response before publication. https://cpj.org/2026/10/cpj-calls-for-re.body: Share this: Share on Bluesky (Opens in new window) Bluesky Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Share on LinkedIn (Opens in new window) LinkedIn Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on WhatsApp (Opens in new window) WhatsApp Email a link to a friend (Opens in new window) Email The Committee to Protect Journalists has joined the October 30 Coalition of human rights organizations in issuing a joint statement marking the International Day of Political Prisoners on October 30. The statement underscores the need for sustained international attention to individual political prisoners, for efforts to secure their release, and for accountability for abuses. More than 300 journalists were imprisoned worldwide as of December 1, 2025, according to CPJ’s latest annual prison census , the fifth consecutive year the count has topped that mark. These persistently high numbers reflect rising authoritarianism and a growing number of armed conflicts worldwide. China has been the world’s worst jailer of journalists for three consecutive years, holding at least 50 in 2025. Myanmar, with 30 held, rose from third place in 2024 to second; Israel, with 29 imprisoned, fell from second to third. Azerbaijan, which imprisoned 24, entered the top 10 for the first time since 2018, nearly doubling its prisoner count from the prior year. The numbers imprisoned in Russia, Belarus, Egypt, and Eritrea were consistent with those of the past five years. Israel, the only country on the worst-jailers list that is traditionally considered a democracy, began rapidly imprisoning Palestinian journalists following the start of the Israel-Gaza war in October 2023. Many are imprisoned on undisclosed charges or held without charge in arbitrary detention, in contravention of international law. While Israeli citizens enjoy a broad array of civil rights and freedoms, legal experts identify a radically different standard of justice for Palestinians in the Occupied Palestinian Territory. Israel has arrested more than 110 Palestinian journalists over the course of the war. Journalists are often held in cruel and life-threatening conditions that one freed Palestinian prisoner likened to “a cemetery of the living.” Many imprisoned journalists endure these dangers for years. More than one-third of the journalists counted in the 2025 census are serving sentences of more than five years. Nearly half have never been sentenced at all, and 26% of that group have languished in jail without a sentence for five years or more. Such detentions violate international law , which requires fair trials without undue delay. To reverse the tide of imprisonments, CPJ has consistently called on governments to uphold the rule of law, stop criminalizing journalists who report factually, and hold power to account. CPJ mobilizes political pressure and international expert interventions , leads solidarity campaigns , and takes legal action . With partners, CPJ works to halt or reform legislation that hinders reporting and puts journalists in legal jeopardy. CPJ also provides direct legal, medical, trauma, and other health-related assistance to a growing number of imprisoned and newly released journalists. Over the past five years, the number of journalists receiving both prison and post-prison support from CPJ has risen by nearly 200%. CPJ reiterates its call on governments to release all imprisoned journalists and to rescind policies or laws that criminalize journalism. The international community must uphold the fundamental right to a free press and take the necessary steps to ensure the safety of journalists, particularly those reporting in conflict zones. https://cpj.org/2026/10/somaliland-detai.body: Share this: Share on Bluesky (Opens in new window) Bluesky Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Share on LinkedIn (Opens in new window) LinkedIn Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on WhatsApp (Opens in new window) WhatsApp Email a link to a friend (Opens in new window) Email New York, October 28, 2026—The Committee to Protect Journalists calls on authorities in the breakaway republic of Somaliland to release journalist Abdirahman Mohamed Ege, who has been held without charge since October 22 in the city of Hargeisa after interviewing a presidential aspirant. “Abdirahman Mohamed Ege has committed no crime, and the fact that he has been arrested for doing his job is a worrying sign that Somaliland authorities do not respect press freedom,” said CPJ Africa Program Coordinator Muthoki Mumo. “Abdirahman should be released unconditionally and without delay.” On the morning of October 22, Abdirahman was summoned to the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) headquarters in Somaliland’s capital, Hargeisa, and detained upon arrival, according to the Somaliland Journalists Association , and Abdikarim Saed Salah, deputy chairperson of Horn Cable TV, where the journalist works, who spoke to CPJ. Abdikarim, who has visited Abdirahman several times in detention, told CPJ that the journalist was being questioned about his October 15 interview with Abdiqadir Sharay, who plans to stand for the presidency of the Federal Government of Somalia in national elections in 2027. Somalia has a tense relationship with Somaliland, which declared independence from Somalia in 1991. Somaliland has not been recognized internationally, except for by Israel in December 2025. Abdiqadir was arrested on October 16 in connection with the interview, according to news reports . Somaliland authorities have cracked down on press freedom over the last year, with numerous arrests of journalists and media workers. Journalist Abdiqani Hussein Abokor is also in detention, having been arrested on August 29 after interviewing a poet. CPJ’s October 26 emails requesting comment from Somaliland’s ministry of information and the office of the president did not receive any responses. https://cpj.org/2026/10/how-journalists-.body: Share this: Share on Bluesky (Opens in new window) Bluesky Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Share on LinkedIn (Opens in new window) LinkedIn Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on WhatsApp (Opens in new window) WhatsApp Email a link to a friend (Opens in new window) Email The 2026 U.S. midterm elections will take place next week amid a constant drumbeat of press freedom violations , ceaseless vitriol against journalists from the Trump administration, and direct threats to the press across the U.S. Globally, elections are risky for journalists, whether reporting from polling sites or working online. Intensifying attacks against journalists in the U.S. mean newsrooms should already be preparing their staff and freelancers not only for Election Day, but what comes next, and in the weeks and months ahead. “Given the dangerous and evolving landscape for press freedom and journalist safety across the U.S., the importance of safety training and resources for journalists in this country has never been greater. We are paying close attention to local journalists, who face greater risk reporting within their communities during a highly polarized time,” says CPJ Chief Emergencies Officer Lucy Westcott. “Whether it’s digital safety best practices, navigating protest coverage, or making sure journalists know where to get mental health support, we’re helping reporters stay safe amid the crushing reality of being a journalist in the U.S. right now.” Five ways journalists can protect themselves while covering midterm elections Click here Australian reporter Lauren Tomasi, of 9News, was hit by a rubber bullet on Sunday while covering protests against mass deportations in Los Angeles. (Screenshot: 9News-ITV News/YouTube) Intensifying attacks against journalists Journalists across the country, regardless of their medium and beat, are operating amid a roiling emergency and daily threats to their profession and safety. Whether holding a camera, a pen, a phone, or a notebook, more than a decade on from the introduction of “fake news” and “enemies of the people” into the national lexicon, there has been a near-total evaporation of the expectation of press safety in the United States. Moments appear like flashes in the spiral of decline: CNN journalist Omar Jimenez and his colleagues being arrested while on-air in Minnesota in 2020, or Australian journalist Lauren Tomasi leaping in pain after being shot by police while reporting live from protests in Los Angeles in 2025. CNN correspondent Omar Jimenez and his colleagues were arrested while on-air while covering protests in Minnesota in 2020. (Screenshot: CNN/YouTube) Those covering the U.S. midterms are reporting within a drastically decaying environment for press freedom and safety. Since the beginning of 2026, 166 press freedom violations have been recorded against journalists by the U.S. Press Freedom Tracker, including arrests, assaults, and the issuing of subpoenas, all connected to their reporting. CPJ has seen a marked increase in requests for physical, digital, and psychosocial safety assistance from U.S.-based journalists, who know this training and knowledge is now crucial to keeping them safe while reporting. In 2021, CPJ supported 34 U.S.-based journalists with safety training and emergency financial support, which swelled to 959 journalists just four years later, a more than 2,000 percent increase. The U.S. Journalist Assistance Network (JAN) was created in 2025 to give an ever-growing number of U.S.-based journalists a fast and direct way to access support, training, and safety information. How CPJ has supported journalist safety in 2026 Declining press freedom in the U.S. and heightened risks for journalists has impacted not only the physical and digital safety of reporters, but also their mental health. Amid intense immigration crackdowns in Minnesota earlier this year, CPJ quickly set up with partners an emergency fund to support more than two dozen local journalists on the frontlines of this coverage with mental health support and personal safety equipment. CPJ has spoken with newsrooms serving diaspora populations who report feeling exhausted and anxious about continued immigration enforcement in their communities. In Minnesota, journalists told CPJ of the disbelief that the violence they witnessed could happen in the cities they call home. Editors covering Minnesota endured 24-hour shifts, reviewing graphic images and testimony, and carrying the colossal weight of caring for their journalists on assignment. CPJ and our partners have long supported journalists in the U.S. with mental health support, and will continue as long as journalists need it. Across the country, CPJ has so far in 2026 provided more than 400 journalists with physical, digital, psychosocial, and legal safety training, including safety workshops focused on this election. Digital safety and intensifying surveillance across internet platforms are primary safety concerns for journalists in the U.S., with nearly 60 percent of CPJ’s 2025 safety training workshops including digital safety as a primary focus. A CNN sticker is seen on equipment in the James Brady press briefing room of the White House on September 19, 2026 in Washington, DC. The White House made good on US President Donald Trump’s vow to deny CNN, MS NOW and Politico access to the presidential mansion as punishment for reporting what he calls “fake news.” The three news outlets denounced the ban as a violation of the US constitution and vowed to keep reporting on the US government. (Photo: AFP/Oliver Contreras) How to shore up press freedom in the U.S. As CPJ continues to keep journalists across the U.S. safe, attacks against the press have taken on an even sharper edge as the midterms have drawn closer. Following the ban on news outlets CNN, MS NOW, and Politico from accessing the White House, CPJ joined a legal effort to restore their access. While it remains in place for now, the ban marks “one of the most aggressive uses of legal powers against the press in the United States in decades,” says Jose Zamora, CPJ’s Americas Regional Director. Similarly, government directives under the Trump administration have been weaponized to crackdown on press freedom, undermine the rule of law, and block Congress from upholding its oversight role in protecting First Amendment rights. Journalists and media outlets have been threatened with retaliation over unfavorable news coverage as part of an intensifying system of repression that lawmakers must move quickly after midterms to dismantle. Intensifying attacks against journalists in the U.S. mean newsrooms should already be preparing their staff and freelancers not only for Election Day, but what comes next, and in the weeks and months ahead. (Photo: Reuters/Nathan Howard) “Tactics to suppress the press that are the hallmarks of authoritarian regimes have become the norm under the current US administration,” said CPJ CEO Jodie Ginsberg. “A free press is a fundamental public good. Those elected to serve the American people need to rediscover a backbone and rigorously defend a free press. Media organizations must equally refuse to be bullied and stand forthright in their defense of the First Amendment.” The litany of government-led attacks against the press has sparked national attention over the past year. At least 10 journalists have been subpoenaed this year in publicly reported cases as the Trump administration has attempted to stem government leaks by using subpoenas to pressure journalists to reveal their sources. Journalists reporting on protests face unprecedented charges, including independent reporters Don Lemon and Georgia Fort, who were arrested along with other journalists while covering a protest in a St. Paul church. They face felony charges, including under the KKK Act that is intended to protect Black Americans’ constitutional rights. Press access continues to be squeezed and shuttered. New and stringen

In a joint statement, rights organizations urged Egyptian authorities to allow Mada Masr to operate freely, and stop weaponizing media permit laws to arrest and prosecute journalists. “The order to shut down Mada Masr, one of Egypt’s leading media outlets, is outrageous and a clear signal that Egypt is doubling down on its efforts to suppress independent media,” said CPJ CEO Jodie Ginsberg. “The world cannot keep watching in silence as Egypt’s independent journalism dies, while Egyptian journalists risk their freedom to keep the public informed.” On October 27, the New Cairo Misdemeanor Court convicted Attalah of managing an unlicensed website and imposed the maximum penalty, a fine of 3 million Egyptian pounds (about US$54,000) and the closure of Mada Masr’s website. Attalah was taken into custody inside the courthouse immediately after the ruling, and released approximately seven hours later. The ruling is part of an unprecedented crackdown on the press in Egypt, which recently saw the arrest of the entire newsroom of the investigative platform Matsadaash, and the summoning of journalist Rasha Azab . Egypt remains one of the world’s worst jailers of journalists, with at least 25 currently behind bars . Read the full statement in English and Arabic . https://www.omct.org/en/resources/urgent.body: Share New information IND 001 / 0426 / OBS 020.1 Threats Surveillance Risk of arbitrary arrest Judicial harrasment / India 28 October 2026 The Observatory for the Protection of Human Rights Defenders, a partnership of the International Federation for Human Rights (FIDH) and the World Organisation Against Torture (OMCT), has received new information and requests your urgent intervention in the following situation in India . New information: The Observatory has been informed about escalating threats, intimidation, and surveillance targeting Mr Shiv Kumar , a prominent labour rights defender from the Dalit community, and a member of the Mazdoor Adhikar Sangathan (MAS), an organisation advocating for the rights of contract workers in Haryana State. On 8 October 2026, at approximately 11 pm, around 10 armed police officers belonging to the National Investigation Agency (NIA) and Haryana Police, some in plain clothes and others in uniform, visited Shiv Kumar’s residence in the village of Devru, in Sonipat district. They searched his home and the surrounding area and inspected the mobile phones of his family members. On 11 October 2026, an unmarked vehicle was seen following Mr Shiv Kumar’s brother, Mr Sagar Kumar, as he was leaving for work. On 10 October 2026, police officers visited a shop near Mr Shiv Kumar’s workplace while NIA officials showed photographs of Mr Shiv Kumar and his colleague Manjeet to people in the area surrounding the MAS office and making enquiries about them. These incidents follow a visit by NIA officials to Mr Shiv Kumar’s residence on 25 September 2026, when he was not at home. The officers allegedly questioned and intimidated his father and brother without presenting a warrant or prior notice. They reportedly took his father’s mobile phone, accessed its contents without his consent and subsequently returned it. The same officials allegedly visited the premises of MAS and questioned and threatened the landlord over the rental of premises to labour rights activists. Following this visit, the landlord reportedly asked Mr Shiv Kumar and his colleagues to vacate the premises. The Observatory recalls that, on 16 April 2026, the NIA issued a notice summoning Mr Shiv Kumar for questioning in connection with the so-called “ Lucknow Conspiracy Case ”, exposing him to a risk of arrest. The case was initiated in September 2023 to investigate alleged attempts to revive Maoist activities in northern India and has involved investigations into human rights defenders, labour rights activists, students and lawyers across several Indian states. The Observatory also recalls that Mr Shiv Kumar has previously been subjected to arbitrary detention and torture. On 12 March 2026, Delhi Police Special Cell officers detained him for approximately 60 hours without a warrant or explanation and subjected him to torture and ill-treatment after questioning him about other activists in connection with the “Lucknow Conspiracy Case”. He was released on the night of 14 to 15 March 2026 following a habeas corpus petition filed by his father before the Delhi High Court. In January 2021, he was also arbitrarily detained and tortured by Haryana Police during farmers’ protests. Subsequent judicial inquiries, including a District and Sessions Judge’s report released on 1 July 2022 confirmed that he had been illegally detained and tortured in police custody. The Observatory further recalls that the prohibition of torture and arbitrary detention is enshrined in Articles 7 and 9 of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR), to which India is a State party. The right to privacy and the right to freedom of association are also protected under Articles 17 and 22 of the ICCPR. The Observatory is gravely concerned by the threats against Mr Shiv Kumar’s family, particularly the alleged use of firearms to intimidate them, the search of his home and inspection of his family members’ mobile phones, as well as the surveillance of his brother. These incidents appear to form part of a broader pattern of intimidation targeting Mr Shiv Kumar and his relatives, further heightening the risk of his arbitrary arrest. The Observatory calls on the Indian authorities to immediately put an end to all acts of harassment, intimidation, and threats against Mr Shiv Kumar, his family and colleagues, and to guarantee that he will not be subjected to arbitrary arrest or detention in connection with his legitimate human rights activities. Actions requested: Please write to the authorities of India urging them to: Guarantee in all circumstances the physical integrity and psychological well-being of Shiv Kumar, his family members, and all human rights defenders in India; Put an immediate end to all acts of intimidation, threats, and surveillance targeting Mr Shiv Kumar, his relatives, and colleagues, and refrain from any arbitrary arrest or detention; Order an independent, impartial and effective investigation into the reported threats, intimidation, and surveillance and ensure that those responsible are held accountable; Ensure that the proceedings in the so-called “Lucknow Conspiracy Case” are conducted in accordance with international human rights standards and are not used to target human rights defenders for their legitimate activities. Guarantee in all circumstances that human rights defenders in India can carry out their legitimate activities freely and safely, without fear of reprisals. Addresses Mr. (Shri) Narendra Modi, Prime Minister, Email : appt.pmo@nic.in , Twitter : @PMOIndia / @narendramodi Dr. Subrahmanyam Jaishankar, Hon'ble Minister of External Affairs, Email : eam@mea.gov.in , X : @MEAIndia / @DrSJaishankar Mr. (Shri) Amit Shah, Union Cabinet Minister of Home Affairs; and Minister of Cooperation, Email : amitshah.mp@mpls.sansad.in, amitshah.bjp@gmail.com , X: @AmitShah Mr. (Shri) Arjun Ram Meghwal, Hon'ble Minister of State of Law and Justice, Email : mljoffice@gov.in , X : @MLJ_GoI Mr. (Shri) Raj Nath Singh, Hon'ble Minister of Defence, Email : rmo@mod.nic.in ; X : @DefenceMinIndia Mr. Arindam Bagghi, Permanent representative of India to the United Nations in Geneva, Email : india.geneva@mea.gov.in Please also write to the diplomatic missions or embassies of India in your respective countries. *** Paris-Geneva , 28 October 2026 Kindly inform us of any action undertaken quoting the code of this appeal in your reply. https://hcnm.osce.org/hcnm/669297.body: Media advisory NGO Education for the 21st Century from Serbia to receive Max van der Stoel Award 2026 Date: 29 October 2026 Place: THE HAGUE Source: OSCE High Commissioner on National Minorities THE HAGUE, 29 October 2026 ‒ The 2026 Max van der Stoel Award will be presented to the NGO NGO non-governmental organization Education for the 21st Century from Serbia at the Peace Palace in The Hague on Tuesday, 3 November. Erik Weststrate, Netherlands Ambassador for International Organizations, will present the award on behalf of the Foreign Affairs Ministry of the Netherlands. Education for the 21st Century from Serbia was selected as the winner of the 2026 Max van der Stoel Award in recognition of its work to promote tolerance, inclusion and respect for diversity through education. Director of Education for the 21st Century Lidija Županić Šuica, OSCE High Commissioner on National Minorities Christophe Kamp and Ambassador Weststrate will address the event. The Max van der Stoel Award has been organized by the High Commissioner on National Minorities and sponsored by the Foreign Affairs Ministry of the Netherlands every two years since 2003. It is awarded to an organization, group or individual in recognition of their extraordinary and outstanding achievements in improving the position of national minorities across the OSCE countries. Recipients of the award receive €50,000. Event material can be found here . The event programme is available here . Media representatives who wish to attend the event at the Peace Palace in The Hague on 3 November 2026 starting at 15:30 should send their name, contact details and the name of the media organization they represent to Michelle Pirotta, michelle.pirotta@osce.org , before 15:30 on 2 November . It will also be possible to follow the ceremony live here . Follow the discussion on X using the hashtag #MvdSAward . https://uzbekistan.osce.org/news/project.body: News News Item OSCE trains law enforcement officials in Uzbekistan on the responsible use of artificial intelligence Issued on: 29 October 2026 Issued by: OSCE Project Co-ordinator in Uzbekistan The OSCE Project Co-ordinator in Uzbekistan, jointly with the Action against Terrorism Unit of the OSCE Transnational Threats Department and in co-operation with the Law Enforcement Academy of the Republic of Uzbekistan, organized a two-day training course on the responsible use of artificial intelligence (AI) in law enforcement. Held on 21–22 October in Tashkent, the training brought together national law enforcement and specialized agencies to explore how AI tools can support their work while safeguarding human rights, protecting sensitive information and ensuring accountability. Opening of the two-day training course on the responsible use of AI in law enforcement As AI continues to create new opportunities for public institutions, its use in law enforcement requires careful consideration of the risks and safeguards involved. AI tools can support information analysis, document preparation, translation and other routine tasks. However, their outputs may contain errors or fabricated information, making professional judgement, independent verification and human oversight essential. “Application of AI in law enforcement requires particular care. The decisions and actions of law enforcement institutions can have significant consequences for individuals and public trust. New technologies must therefore be used in ways that uphold human rights, protect sensitive information and ensure appropriate human oversight,” - said Ambassador Antti Karttunen, the OSCE Project Co-ordinator in Uzbekistan, in his opening remarks. Over the two days, participants explored practical applications of AI in law enforcement, including document analysis, reporting and information retrieval. The training addressed information security risks, particularly the risks of entering operational, personal or confidential information into publicly available AI tools. Participants also learned about locally run AI models as a potential alternative for handling sensitive information in more secure environments. Participants also examined the legal safeguards for responsible AI use, including in counter-terrorism, and the INTERPOL–UNICRI Toolkit for Responsible AI Innovation in Law Enforcement. Practical exercises focused on effective prompting, verifying AI-generated outputs and applying human oversight and accountability. The training was supported through OSCE Secretariat’s Project CLEAR (Critical Thinking, Information and Media Literacy, Ethical AI, and Resilience for Preventing and Countering Violent Extremism and Radicalization that Lead to Terrorism), funded by Finland, Germany, Norway and the United States. Project CLEAR supports participating States in strengthening comprehensive and human-rights-compliant approaches to preventing and countering violent extremism and radicalization that lead to terrorism that manifest in, and stem from, online environments and the misuse of the internet, emerging technologies, and AI for terrorist purposes across the OSCE area. The training also demonstrated cross-dimensional co-operation within the OSCE, bringing together the politico-military and economic and environmental dimensions. This co-operation highlights the importance of addressing the opportunities and challenges of artificial intelligence through an integrated approach that considers both security and economic and environmental aspects. News News Item Shaping Future Initiatives: Young People Discuss Peace and Security in Tashkent Issued on: 29 October 2026 Issued by: OSCE Project Co-ordinator in Uzbekistan Direct dialogue and shared experiences are essential for young people to contribute meaningfully to peace and security in their communities. For participants of recent OSCE initiatives - from the Model OSCE in Tashkent to cross-border dialogues in the Fergana Valley - these platforms offer a space to exchange ideas and turn their perspectives into practical contributions. Building on these efforts, the OSCE Project Co-ordinator in Uzbekistan organized the Model OSCE Alumni Meeting on 20 October in Tashkent. Bringing together alumni of the Model OSCE alongside young people involved in other OSCE youth activities, including the Young Peacebuilders Cross-Border Initiative, the gathering served as a follow-up consultation to reflect on their experiences and discuss prospects for future collaboration. Discussions focused on overcoming barriers to youth engagement, exploring potential grassroots initiatives, and identifying possible areas for further cooperation, building on the outcomes and lessons learned from previous initiatives. Group photo of participants at the Model OSCE Alumni Meeting in Tashkent, bringing together young peacebuilders and decision-makers Highlighting the practical impact of the Young Peacebuilders Cross-Border Initiative in the Fergana Valley, Anastasiya Shikina, Co-Chair of the Youth Sounding Board established by support of the Delegation of the European Union to Uzbekistan, emphasized: “Young people should not be seen simply as an audience for discussions on peace and security, but as partners who can help shape them. Through this initiative, young people from Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, and Tajikistan developed concrete recommendations on building trust, countering misinformation, and addressing shared environmental challenges. Meaningful participation is about having the opportunity to influence what happens next.” For Otabek Turgunboev, who participated in the first edition of Model OSCE in Uzbekistan in 2024, diplomatic simulations complement field experience by developing critical negotiating skills. “Since then, my engagement with diplomacy, preventive diplomacy, and youth participation in peace and security has continued to grow,” Otabek noted. “Looking back, I see the value of initiatives like Model OSCE not only in the skills they teach, but also in the questions they leave you with long after the simulation ends.” The insights, innovative recommendations, and practical proposals shared during the meeting highlighted key priorities and opportunities for advancing the Youth, Peace and Security agenda. By connecting youth, the event reaffirmed the importance of sustained spaces for meaningful youth engagement with decision-makers to strengthen inclusive approaches to peace and security. https://rsf.org/fr/philippines-rsf-d%C3%.body: Philippines : RSF dénonce une nouvelle tentative d’intimidation judiciaire contre la presse après l’arrestation du journaliste Philip Lustre Jr. Organisation : RSF_fr Partager facebook twitter linkedin Courriel Reporters sans frontières (RSF) condamne l’arrestation du journaliste chevronné Philip Lustre Jr., brièvement détenu sans avoir été informé des motifs des poursuites engagées contre lui, avant d’être libéré sous caution. Alors que plusieurs journalistes de GMA Network font également l’objet de poursuites pour diffamation, RSF exhorte les autorités philippines à mettre fin à l’instrumentalisation de la justice contre la presse. Le 24 octobre, Philip Lustre Jr. , un journaliste de 72 ans, qui a notamment collaboré avec le Philippine Daily Inquirer , a été arrêté alors qu’il assistait à un forum de presse à Quezon City, dans l’agglomération de Manille, au nord des Philippines. Conduit dans un commissariat, il n’a été informé ni des motifs des poursuites engagées contre lui ni de l’identité du plaignant. L’adresse figurant sur le mandat d’arrêt ne correspondait pas à son domicile, soulevant de nouvelles interrogations sur la nature de la plainte. Le journaliste a versé une caution de 48 000 pesos philippins (près de 700 euros) et a été libéré plus tard dans la soirée. Il a toutefois fallu deux jours à son avocat pour établir que le plaignant était Manases « Mans » Carpio, l’époux de la vice-présidente Sara Duterte. Philip Lustre Jr. est poursuivi en vertu de l’article 4(c)(4) de la loi sur la prévention de la cybercriminalité, qui réprime la diffamation en ligne, dite “cyberdiffamation”. La plainte porte sur une publication Facebook de Philip Lustre Jr. datant de mars 2026. Le journaliste, qui a mené de nombreuses enquêtes sur la famille Duterte, s’y interrogeait sur une éventuelle participation de Manases Carpio au financement d’un réseau présumé d’anciens militaires chargés de distribuer à des proches du président Ferdinand Marcos Jr. des fonds détournés de projets de lutte contre les inondations. Les avocats du journaliste ont qualifié cette arrestation d’“illégale et irrégulière” et averti que cette procédure risquait d’avoir un “effet dissuasif” sur la liberté de la presse. Journaliste depuis plus de 50 ans, Philip Lustre Jr. a publié en 2023 Kill, Kill, Kill, un livre d’enquête consacré aux crimes commis dans le cadre de la guerre contre la drogue menée sous la présidence de Rodrigo Duterte, père de Sara Duterte et beau-père de Manases Carpio. Une édition actualisée de l’ouvrage est parue en février 2026. “Il est extrêmement préoccupant que Philip Lustre Jr. ait été arrêté sans être informé des accusations portées contre lui, en particulier dans un pays où les procédures judiciaires sont fréquemment instrumentalisées contre la presse. Nous appelons les autorités, et notamment le ministère de la Justice, à abandonner les poursuites à contre lui, à fournir des explications complètes sur ce grave manque de transparence et à prendre des mesures concrètes pour garantir que les journalistes puissent rapporter les faits sans craindre de représailles. Cédric Alviani Directeur du bureau Asie-Pacifique de RSF La famille Duterte multiplie les plaintes pour diffamation contre des journalistes de GMA Network L’arrestation de Philip Lustre Jr. intervient peu après le dépôt de plaintes pour diffamation par un autre membre de la famille de l’ancien président Rodrigo Duterte contre des dirigeants et des journalistes de GMA Network , l’un des principaux groupes audiovisuels privés des Philippines. Le 23 octobre, Paolo Duterte, député de Davao et frère de la vice-présidente Sara Duterte, a déposé des plaintes pour diffamation, notamment en ligne , contre le président du groupe Felipe Gozon , son directeur général Gilberto Duavit Jr. , les présentateurs Mel Tiangco , Vicky Morales et Emil Sumangil , ainsi que les journalistes Darlene Cay , Marvin Parado et Joel San Luis . Ces plaintes font suite à la diffusion d’informations faisant état de transferts présumés d’argent à des membres de la famille Duterte. Dans un reportage diffusé le 25 septembre, GMA Network avait relayé les déclarations d’un ancien policier affirmant avoir remis des valises remplies d’argent à plusieurs membres de cette famille. Les Philippines figurent parmi les pays les plus dangereux au monde pour les professionnels des médias et occupent la 114e place sur 180 pays et territoires au Classement mondial de la liberté de la presse 2026 de RSF . https://montenegro.osce.org/news/mission.body: News News Item OSCE Regional Trial Monitoring conference highlights importance of sustained implementation of justice reforms across the Western Balkans Issued on: 28 October 2026 Issued by: OSCE Mission to Montenegro Fields of work: Rule of law Effective case handling, institutional co-operation and transparency are key to translating justice reforms into lasting practices across the Western Balkans. These issues were at the centre of a three-day regional judicial conference held in Budva from 26 to 28 October, which marked the launch of the second public report under the OSCE’s Regional Trial Monitoring Project. The conference, From Paper to Practice: Making Justice Reforms Work in Organized Crime and Corruption Cases , brought together around 150 judicial and prosecutorial representatives and justice practitioners during the first two days, followed by around 60 civil society representatives on the third day. In addition, the OSCE Mission in Montenegro facilitated the participation of nine students of the Faculty of Law of the University of Montenegro. The second public report builds on findings from the previous monitoring cycle and contributes to ongoing discussions on strengthening justice systems across the region. At the opening of the conference, Stephan Nunner, Deputy Director of the OSCE Conflict Prevention Centre emphasized that the project’s findings and recommendations were only the starting point. “Ownership and implementation are up to stakeholders involved in the justice sector. Effective justice requires an effective justice chain”. He also stressed that reforms should go hand-in-hand with implementation, and “transparency can strengthen public confidence, while international partners can support necessary reforms.” Elsa Papageorgiou, Programme Manager for the Rule of Law in the Western Balkans at European Commission’s DG ENEST, said that sustainable reform depends on ownership, operational clarity, continuity, and the capacity of institutions to absorb and maintain change over time. “Proper handling of organized crime and corruption cases requires well-prepared indictments, sound evidence, efficient proceedings, strong co-ordination among institutions, and outcomes that are procedurally robust and meaningful,” said Papageorgiou. In his closing remarks, Giovanni Gabassi, Deputy Head of the OSCE Mission to Montenegro, stressed that trial monitoring should not only identify shortcomings, but also help address systemic problems through practical recommendations and follow-up. “An important role also belongs to civil society in this process through independent monitoring, evidence-based advocacy, and constructive dialogue with justice institutions,” said Gabassi. The discussions underscored the importance of sustained institutional efforts to turn reforms into practice, supported by evidence-based monitoring, transparency, co-ordination among justice institutions, and constructive engagement with civil society. Over the past two years, the project has monitored more than 350 cases and 4,000 hearings across six Western Balkan jurisdictions. In Montenegro, the OSCE Mission’s Regional Trial Monitoring Project team monitored 1,018 hearings in 61 cases and held nearly 100 meetings and consultations with justice-sector stakeholders. The project is funded by the European Commission through the Instrument for Pre-Accession Assistance and implemented by OSCE field operations in Belgrade, Podgorica, Pristina, Sarajevo, Skopje and Tirana. News News Item Newly qualified youth workers bring skills to communities across Montenegro Issued on: 29 October 2026 Issued by: OSCE Mission to Montenegro Fields of work: Youth Seven youth initiatives engaged more than 100 young people across Montenegro, putting into practice the skills acquired by 15 participants in the Youth Vocational Programme. Supported by the OSCE Mission to Montenegro and implemented by NGO NGO non-governmental organization Forum MNE, the programme culminated in all 15 participants to earn a nationally recognized vocational qualification. As the only accredited educational programme in the field of youth work in Montenegro, the Youth Activist Programme combines theoretical training with practical experience, helping participants strengthen their skills and contribute to the professionalization of youth work. Between February and April 2026, participants, representing civil society organizations, youth services, educational institutions and other organizations working with young people across Montenegro, completed three training modules covering youth work, youth policy, activism and project management. From July to September, they put their learning into practice by designing and implementing seven initiatives that engaged young people through creative, intercultural and community-based activities. Ms. Jelena Novićević, executive director of Forum MNE, emphasized that the greatest value of this programme lies in building a stronger community of professional youth workers and supporting a new generation of curious and motivated practitioners. “Seeing them turn their knowledge and ideas into meaningful activities, created not just for young people but together with them, is what makes this experience so valuable,” said Novićević The participants’ achievements were celebrated at the Youth Activists Festival, organized by Forum MNE on 22 October in Podgorica. The event brought together around 70 youth work practitioners, institutional representatives, civil society organizations and young people. It featured presentations of the seven initiatives, a discussion on youth work as a profession, an intergenerational exchange, a certificate ceremony and an exhibition showcasing the initiatives. Reflecting on the programme, participant Mr. Marko Vukčević highlighted, “This programme has been significant in providing me with education and tools needed for higher quality youth work, as well as with a work qualification that is going to be helpful in gaining employment.
